meta.title: poLight XR Timeline Map
meta.subtitle: Supplier signals from poLight, Q Tech, CML, Optotune and the module chain, dated against Meta, Apple, Samsung/Google, Snap, Xreal and other 2026-2027 launches, with lead-time norms applied backwards from each window.
meta.foot: Sources: poLight/Q Tech filings and decks, patent registers, Meta developer docs, press and broker notes as captured in the dataset (704 events, 108 windows after de-duplication). Phase bands apply generic 3-18-month industry norms, not disclosed schedules. poLight has never named Meta or said '2027'; the DBS 1H27 sentence is unverified; LinkedIn and forum items are circumstantial.

lanes.name: Meta
lanes.blurb: Meta Platforms / Reality Labs: Quest headsets, Ray-Ban/Oakley/Meta-brand AI glasses with EssilorLuxottica, Meta Ray-Ban Display and the Orion AR prototype. Every camera glasses shipped to date is fixed-focus; the spring-2027 Meta VR Glasses (ex-Phoenix) are the first Meta consumer device whose passthrough cameras are documented as autofocus, making Meta the single most important potential top-tier customer for a tunable-lens or VCM autofocus supplier. Meta Connect 2026 (2026-09-23/24) announced Meta VR Glasses for a spring-2027 launch, the central product for the poLight question; see the Meta file. Included here only as calendar intersections. Meta appears only indirectly: poLight's Q3 2025 deck credits Ray-Ban Meta (>2M units in 2024) as the consumer driver, and the user's brief places a Meta autofocus-camera 'VR Glasses' launch in spring 2027. No poLight document names Meta. Meta as producer: display-side Butterscotch varifocal prototype (2023) and the 2026-09-23 announcement of VR glasses for spring 2027, which falls days after Meta's lens-barrel patent publication and Optotune's glasses-class lens launch. Meta's glasses lineup (Ray-Ban Meta Gen 1/2, Oakley HSTN/Vanguard, Ray-Ban Display, Meta Glasses) all carry 12 MP fixed-focus cameras per teardowns; capacity constraints and doubling plans in early 2026. The Meta VR Glasses announced for spring 2027 are the product window that Q Tech's 2H26/2027 ramp and DBS's 1H27 claim would fit. Meta as a producer: the research brief posits 'VR glasses' with autofocus cameras in spring 2027. The 2022-07 / 2023-02 patent priority dates imply a 3.5–4.5-year priority-to-product lag, consistent with reliability qualification during 2024 and production readiness by April 2025. Product verification is outside this file's scope. Meta announced its ~100 g Meta VR Glasses at Connect 2026 (23 Sept 2026) for spring 2027 at USD 1,299.99, with developer specs confirming color stereoscopic 26-PPD passthrough 'with autofocus and depth sensing' but naming no actuator or supplier. Also the dominant AI-glasses OEM (Ray-Ban Display, ~94% share H1 2026).

lanes.name: Apple
lanes.blurb: Apple ships only Vision Pro (2024-02-02; M5 refresh 2025-10-22) and has no glasses yet. Gurman/Kuo put the display-less N50 glasses (two cameras: capture + computer vision) at a WWDC June 2027 unveil, Q2 2027 mass production and late-2027 shipment, after slipping from end-2026. Apple is the most-cited alternative to Meta as poLight's "Top Tier U.S. Consumer Electronics OEM", but no camera-module or focus-actuator vendor is public and the camera configuration was still undecided in July 2026. Apple WWDC 2026 (week of June 8) is listed only as a calendar intersection; see the Apple file. Apple Vision Pro (12 cameras, no module supplier identified in teardown) and the rumored N50 smart glasses with two cameras, originally slated for Dec-2026 mass production/early-2027 launch and later pushed to late 2027 per Bloomberg. No supplier or autofocus detail reported. Apple's tunable-lens filings (2018, 2023, 2024; inventors including ex-CML CTO Richard Topliss) are for fluid-filled see-through prescription lenses in head-mounted devices, not camera autofocus. No Apple glasses-camera AF tunable-lens filing surfaced; Apple camera architect Patrick Llull moved to Meta in May 2026. Strongest alternative identity for poLight's unnamed top-tier U.S. OEM if not Meta; Vision Pro sold ~390k in 2024 and first lighter smart glasses are reported for late 2027. Q Tech's lack of Apple exposure argues against Apple being the Q Tech-backed customer.

lanes.name: Google / Android XR
lanes.blurb: Google owns the Android XR platform (announced 2024-12-12) and co-designs the first glasses, but Samsung builds the hardware (SM-O200P/J) and Xreal builds Aura. Roadmap: audio/camera AI glasses fall/November 2026, display glasses 2027, Gucci/Kering 2027. Google is a U.S. OEM in name, but camera-module sourcing for the 2026 glasses runs through Samsung's supply chain; no AF/actuator disclosure found. Google I/O 2026 (May 19–20) carried Android XR glasses updates; Google also bought part of HTC's XR team ($250M, Jan 2025) and partners with Magic Leap and Samsung. Included here only as calendar/cross-link intersections; see the Google file. Google / Android XR is an alternative OEM or ecosystem candidate (possibly for poLight's platform-style NOK 5m AR camera project), with 2026 audio and display glasses built with Samsung, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster.

lanes.name: Samsung
lanes.blurb: Samsung is the hardware lead of the Android XR alliance: Galaxy XR shipped 2025-10-31 (US$1,799.99) and display-less intelligent eyewear (Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1, single 12MP camera) was introduced 2026-07-22 and FCC-cleared for a November 2026 launch; a micro-LED display model ("Haean") is expected 2027. Any focus actuator in these glasses would most plausibly come from Samsung's smartphone (SEMCO-centred) VCM chain; nothing ties poLight, CML, Optotune, Alps or Q Tech to Samsung glasses, and Samsung is not a U.S. OEM. Samsung introduced Android XR 'intelligent eyewear' (AR1 Gen1, Gentle Monster / Warby Parker frames) at Unpacked London 2026-07-22 with availability 'this fall'; the Feb 2026 Unpacked showed no glasses. Details are in the Samsung/Google file; included here only as calendar intersections.

lanes.name: Snap
lanes.blurb: Snap has shipped camera glasses since 2016 and AR-display Spectacles since 2021; its first consumer AR product, Specs (US$2,195, 51° FOV, 2 RGB + 2 IR cameras), opened pre-orders 2026-09-16 with shipping 'later this fall' 2026 in the US, UK and France. Snap has never published camera megapixels, focus type, or any camera-module/actuator supplier, so Specs is a timing-only candidate for poLight's unnamed 2026 consumer AR/MR customer. Snap revealed consumer Specs at AWE USA 2026-06-16 ($2,195, ships 'this fall') and held a dedicated SPECS launch event 2026-09-16. Included here only as calendar intersections; see the Snap file. Snap's SPECS standalone AR glasses ship fall 2026 at $2,195 with Qualcomm; a low-probability alternative U.S. OEM candidate in the thread.

lanes.name: Xreal
lanes.blurb: Xreal builds Project Aura, the tethered optical see-through Android XR glasses announced at I/O 2025 and opened for reservation at AWE 2026 (price <= US$1,500, fall 2026). Aura carries two tracking cameras and one high-resolution camera with no autofocus mentioned, so it is not a likely TLens host. Xreal is the birdbath display-glasses volume leader (133,700 units in 2025) and filed for a HKEX listing in April 2026 with Luxshare as a shareholder. Its only shipping camera, the Eye module, is documented as fixed-focus; its fall-2026 Android XR glasses Aura carry one undisclosed high-resolution camera, making Aura the only Xreal product where an autofocus lens is plausible. Xreal is a competing display-glasses OEM used as a volume and power comparable (133,731 glasses sold in 2025; Xreal Eye 12 MP camera, phone-powered).

lanes.name: Rokid
lanes.blurb: Rokid sells waveguide AI+AR glasses (Rokid Glasses, Kickstarter Aug 2025) and display-free Ai Glasses Style (Jan 2026), both with a single 12MP Sony IMX681 camera that a July 2026 review measured as fixed focus (34 cm minimum). No autofocus actuator or module supplier is disclosed, so Rokid is an unlikely poLight match.

lanes.name: RayNeo / TCL
lanes.blurb: TCL's RayNeo brand ships the highest volume of Air birdbath glasses and a microLED waveguide line (X2, X3 Pro) with 12MP IMX681 cameras whose focus type has never been stated. Its V3 camera glasses were announced at CES 2025 with 'optical image stabilization', which would imply a lens actuator, but no V3 ship date has been found. TCL's RayNeo launched X3 Pro micro-LED waveguide AR glasses (CES 2025 announce, China sale June 2025, international 2025-12-17 at $1,299) with a 12 MP Sony IMX681 main camera and no stated autofocus. 2026 activity so far is a Project eSIM prototype at CES 2026.

lanes.name: Even Realities
lanes.blurb: Even Realities makes deliberately camera-free display glasses (G1 2024, G2 Nov 2025) and raised US$150m at a US$1bn valuation in July 2026. The CEO has ruled out both a 2026 next-gen launch and cameras, so the lane is a cadence comparable with no autofocus relevance.

lanes.name: Amazon
lanes.blurb: Amazon's wearables went from audio-only Echo Frames (2019–2023) to camera-and-HUD delivery-driver glasses unveiled 2025-10-22, with 5,000 more units in 2026 and 20,000+ by end-2027. The driver use case (barcode scanning at arm's length plus doorstep photos) is a natural variable-focus application, and the rumoured consumer 'Jayhawk' camera glasses (late 2026/early 2027) would be a volume programme, but no camera or actuator supplier is disclosed.

lanes.name: Alibaba Quark
lanes.blurb: Alibaba is the fastest-cadence large glasses OEM: Quark S1/G1 (2025-11-27, 12 MP Sony IMX681 fixed-focus) → Qwen rebrand at MWC (2026-03-02) → N1/N1 Pro with a 50 MP sensor (unveiled 2026-09-22, on sale 2026-10-13). The N1's large sensor makes autofocus more valuable than on 12 MP peers, but no AF wording or module supplier has surfaced.

lanes.name: Xiaomi
lanes.blurb: Xiaomi was poLight's first commercial customer (Mitu Children's Watch 4Pro, 2020-01-07, 8 MP TLens camera) and now ships Xiaomi AI Glasses (2025-06-26, 12 MP IMX681 fixed-focus, Goertek ODM) with a reported 28% China share in Q1 2026. A second generation is rumoured for Q4 2026–2027 (denied); whether it adds AF is unknown. Xiaomi's Mi MIX Fold (2021) was the first flagship phone with a liquid lens, supplied by Swiss startup NEXTLENS (Dietikon, founded 2017); it is a smartphone camera design-in, with no XR relevance found.

lanes.name: Other producers
lanes.blurb: Other producers referenced in the Meta file: Valve's Steam Frame (Sept 2026, monochrome passthrough) appears only as the comparison point in Road to VR's spec table against Meta VR Glasses. Covers Viture (birdbath glasses, Luma Ultra RGB camera, enterprise Helix 12MP glasses shipping Q1 2027, two US$100m rounds) plus minor AI-glasses makers Meizu, INMO, Brilliant Labs, Halliday and Mentra. None of these disclose an autofocus camera or a lens-actuator supplier; several are explicitly fixed-focus or camera-free. Covers Huawei (12 MP AI Glasses 2026-04-20), Lenovo, HTC (VIVE Eagle), Pico/ByteDance (Space Pro slipped to Q4 2026), Valve (Steam Frame shipped 2026-09-18), Sony, Microsoft/Anduril (IVAS → SBMC with Meta), Baidu, Vuzix and Magic Leap, plus generic industry calendar events. None of these shipping glasses advertises autofocus; all use roughly 12–16 MP fixed-focus ultra-wide modules, and none shows a public link to poLight or competing actuator suppliers. Enterprise and demo AR/MR devices confirmed to use TLens: Magic Leap 2 (Yole teardown), SnkeXR medical glasses, a repeat high-end MR HMD, and Ant Group 'Look to Pay' demo glasses. These prove shipping AR integration but are not top-tier consumer glasses. Other producers referenced for context: Microsoft (HoloLens manufacturing ended Dec 2024, ruling it out as the 'US M brand') and Bigscreen (20k+ lifetime units of a ~107 g premium VR headset, a volume comparable).

lanes.name: poLight (TLens)
lanes.blurb: poLight's qualification customer is a "Top Tier U.S. Consumer Electronics OEM"; the 2025-10-13 PO was explicitly for the design of a TLens camera for AR applications, and a follow-on order puts deliveries likely in H2 2026. Among Apple, Google and Samsung, only Apple and Google are U.S. companies, and neither has any public autofocus or actuator disclosure for their glasses; the H2 2026 delivery window lines up better with Meta than with Apple's Q2-2027 mass production. poLight's disclosed AR design wins are Vuzix Shield (industrial, dual TLens autofocus cameras, April 2024) and SnkeXR (medical, Oct 2025), plus an unnamed consumer-electronics AR/MR device with a NOK 2.4m follow-on order (April 2026) and a 'first consumer AR/MR design-in' disclosed in August 2026 for a 2026 launch. None of the six OEMs in this file has a public link to poLight. Only historical design-in evidence in this scope: Yole records Xiaomi's Mitu 4Pro (Jan 2020) as the first commercial TLens product. No link from poLight to any of the glasses OEMs covered here was found. poLight ASA (Oslo Børs: PLT) sells the TLens piezo-MEMS tunable lens, already inside enterprise AR/MR cameras (Magic Leap 2, Vuzix Shield, SnkeXR). Three separate consumer AR|MR programs are public: Program A (Q Tech-backed top-tier U.S. OEM qualification, POs Aug 2025/Feb 2026/Jun 2026), Program B (leading consumer OEM, reclassified as first consumer design-in on 2026-07-10 with launch expected 2026) and Program C (NOK 5m AR camera design for a top-tier U.S. OEM). poLight never names Meta and has never stated 2027. poLight reference points found in this file: invited SPIE AR/VR/MR talks in 2025 and 2026 (where CML was absent), the Q Tech partnership backed by a 'US top-tier customer' and TLens's '<6 mW' power claim used as the benchmark against CML SMA. poLight (fabless, Norway) makes the TLens PZT-piezo tunable lens; ST fabs the actuator wafers and Asian partners assemble. AR2025 reports no new MEMS wafers ordered in 2025, 55% of deliveries to AR/MR, and three POs tied to a Top-Tier U.S. consumer OEM AR program; a fresh ST wafer order would be a leading indicator of a volume ramp. poLight ASA (Oslo), maker of the TLens piezo-MEMS autofocus lens fabbed at ST's Agrate fab. Its releases track qualification orders from the Q Tech-linked top-tier US OEM (Aug 2025, Oct 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026), a separate first consumer AR/MR design-in (Aug 2026), and the progress of the Q Tech TLens line; the only teardown-confirmed XR win is Magic Leap 2. poLight's own IP (2006 → 2025, including the Phair and Tallaron patents cited by Meta), its SPIE invited talks in Jan 2025 and Jan 2026, and the Oct 2025 – Sep 2026 order stream from an unnamed top-tier US consumer OEM for TLens cameras in AR head-worn devices, including a qualification-program PO and a mass-price strategic TLens PO. Recent filings (lead-free TLens, low-power driver) point at consumer-qualification requirements. Norwegian supplier of the TLens piezo-MEMS tunable-lens autofocus (TLens Silver, Add-In, PD50 driver) and TWedge. Runs three separate consumer programs: the Q Tech-backed top-tier U.S. OEM qualification (A), the Oct-2025 ~NOK 5m AR head-worn camera project (B) and the 2026 consumer AR/MR design-in (C). poLight has never named Meta.

lanes.name: Q Technology
lanes.blurb: Q Technology, poLight's strategic investor and module partner. The only Meta link in this file is a Xueqiu forum post asserting Q Tech supplies Quest tracking/passthrough modules and that its TLens tie-up positions it for Meta glasses; no HKEX/IR primary source exists. Q Technology (HK:1478) bought 32.97% of poLight in April 2025 'with backing from a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer' and built a dedicated TLens assembly/test line (equipment installed Oct 2025, lenses qualified by Aug 2026, NRE invoiced USD 313k + 179k). Its FY2025 deck places TLens and TWedge on a 2026 XR roadmap, making it the module-level bridge between poLight and the unnamed OEM. Q Technology is simultaneously poLight's largest shareholder and TLens production partner, and (via its controlling shareholder) the new owner of TDK's camera-module actuator business with 2,000+ patents and SMA routes. Its FY2025 deck puts TLens on the 2026 roadmap and targets Top-2 actuator rank, so a Q Tech-built XR camera module could use either technology. Q Technology invested NOK 171.5 M in poLight on 2025-04-15 'backed by a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer' and is building a dedicated TLens assembly/test line in China; poLight invoiced USD 313,141 of NRE in March 2026 for qualifying it for mass production, with work continuing through 2026. Q Technology (1478.HK), Kunshan camera-module maker and poLight's largest shareholder (~30%), building a dedicated TLens assembly-and-test line and, via its controlling shareholder, absorbing TDK's actuator unit (Actutek). Its semi-annual decks give the only dated primary-source ladder from "US M brand vendor code" (Aug 2024) to "TLens volume delivery achieved" and "Overseas Key Customers ramp 2H26/2027" (Aug 2026), but no filing names Meta. Q Technology, poLight's manufacturing partner: Chris Liu (GM Q Tech IoT BU since Oct 2021) and Louis So sit on poLight's board, and the Q3-2025 deck reports a TLens assembly and final-test line at Q Tech under process qualification, with initial lens yield 'not so bad' by Q1 2026. Relevant as the capacity leg of any top-tier OEM design-in. Camera-module maker and poLight's largest shareholder (~NOK 171m, ~one-third stake since June 2025), backed by a top-tier U.S. customer; building a dedicated TLens assembly/test line. Holds a 'US M brand' XR vendor code since 2024 and absorbed TDK's actuator business, so it could supply Meta with VCM or TLens modules.

lanes.name: Cambridge Mechatronics
lanes.blurb: Cambridge Mechatronics (UK) designs SMA wire actuators, controller ICs and firmware, licensed to Alps Alpine, GalaxyCore, TDK and others, shipping in 100M+ smartphones. It is the most credible mechanical alternative to poLight's TLens for autofocus in glasses, with a five-year trail of anonymous 'commercial engagements' with US tech giants in AR/VR, a 2026 deformable-lens patent for glasses/headsets and a job ad citing 'AI glasses' — but no named XR customer, order or production disclosure. Cambridge Mechatronics: SMA actuator maker with 'commercial engagements with US technology giants' since Oct 2021, SPIE XR talks in 2022–2023, a $40m raise in 2024, and 2024-priority filings (WO2025186538/9, WO2026087900) for SMA-deformed liquid/gel lenses in AR/VR headsets. Meta's SMA-flavoured two-stage-actuator application citing CML was allowed then abandoned in May 2025. Ex-CML CTOs Topliss and Brown now appear at Apple. Cambridge Mechatronics, the strongest competitor candidate: SMA AF+OIS actuators in mass production via licensees (Alps Alpine), Zero Hold Power, and a 2026 deformable-liquid-lens application. Its patents appear in Meta filings and it cites 'US technology giant' engagements, but its licensing model leaves no public order trail; SMA versus piezo is the key technical distinction.

lanes.name: Optotune
lanes.blurb: Optotune's EL-3.1-10.8 electromagnetically-actuated liquid lens appears only as a reference row from the brief (20 mW @10 dpt, 1.72 mm thick, ms response, datasheet listing AR/VR); not re-verified here. Optotune (Dietikon, CH) makes voice-coil-actuated shape-changing liquid lenses and is the only tunable-lens rival with a glasses-class part: EL-3.1-10.8 (1.72 mm, 0.3 g, 3.1 mm CA, 20 mW @10 dpt), launched 2026-09-21 but documented for OEMs since 2025-09-17. No XR design win, financing or XR talk found; its AR page promises custom lenses to volume production. Optotune's liquid-lens filings target smart-glasses and AR/VR optics (ring-actuated lens 2023, gravity-coma compensation 2024). Its US20160202455A1 was cited by the EP search report against Meta's lens-barrel family. No Optotune camera-AF presence at SPIE AR/VR/MR 2025–2026. Swiss tunable-lens maker whose EL-3.1-10.8 electromagnetic liquid lens (1.7 mm, 0.3 g, 20-85 mW) launched Sept 2026 targeting AR/VR OEM integration. The clearest identifiable direct technological alternative to TLens, though with higher power consumption.

lanes.name: Corning Varioptic
lanes.blurb: Corning Varioptic (Lyon) sells electrowetting liquid lenses positioned explicitly 'for industrial applications'; packaged parts are ≥3.5 mm thick. Corning's AR role is high-index waveguide glass, not autofocus, and its 2026-27 event calendar is entirely machine vision. Corning Varioptic electrowetting liquid lenses offer barrel-free autofocus but are positioned for industrial, scientific and medical vision rather than consumer AR; no public Meta link was found. poLight names Corning among its tunable-optics competitors.

lanes.name: Sheba Microsystems
lanes.blurb: Sheba Microsystems (Toronto) offers MEMS sensor-shift autofocus (<10 mW, <5 ms) and launched an AR/VR/XR headset camera on 2024-01-09, but had 17 staff and USD 400K sales in 2026 with no disclosed customers. A June-2026 COO hire signals an industrialization push. Sheba Microsystems offers MEMS sensor-shift autofocus for compact AR/VR cameras; its June 2026 Teledyne MEMS partnership concerns ADAS cameras, not glasses. Judged low-probability for the Meta socket given limited consumer-volume maturity.

lanes.name: VCM / SMA actuator makers
lanes.blurb: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO) designs and makes camera lenses and actuators in-house and in December 2025 was reported close to its first FP-coil (AF/OIS actuator component) supply to an unnamed "global big tech" whose profile matches Apple, with "potential expansion to XR devices". This is the only actuator-supply signal found around the three OEMs and points to conventional VCM, not tunable lenses. VCM is poLight's named primary competitor ('very tough competition from VCM'). Q Tech's controlling shareholder is acquiring TDK's micro-actuator (VCM) assets, so Q Tech can offer both VCM and TLens camera modules to the same OEM. Conventional VCM/SMA actuator makers: Alps Alpine (CML-licensed SMA mass production since Jan 2023, piezo zoom), MinebeaMitsumi (AF VCM since 2005), TDK's camera-actuator unit (carved out as Actutek, incl. SMA 'memory metal' IP, sold to Q Tech's controlling shareholder) and Korean OIS suppliers. No public evidence of any supplying autofocus actuators for XR glasses. VCM/SMA actuator makers; here the TDK camera-module actuator business (Micro Actuator Solutions) carved into Actutek and acquired by Q Tech's controlling shareholder between April 2025 and June 2026. Shows the Q Tech group now offers VCM/OIS alternatives alongside TLens, so a Q Tech module does not by itself imply TLens. Incumbent conventional actuator makers (MinebeaMitsumi VCM since 2005, Alps Alpine VCM and CML-licensed SMA, TDK's actuator business now in the Q Tech group). Meta patents also describe VCM solutions, so a conventional actuator remains a ~10% alternative in the thread's estimates.

lanes.name: Camera-module & assembly chain
lanes.blurb: Camera-module and assembly chain around Meta: Goertek (Quest, Ray-Ban Meta, Display engine, reportedly Phoenix), Luxshare (Vietnam VR line), Sunny Optical (camera modules), EssilorLuxottica assembly. Analyst and press supply-chain maps place the fixed-focus AI-glasses cameras with Sunny; no source yet names the autofocus camera module or actuator vendor for the 2027 VR Glasses. Camera-module and assembly chain evidence for these OEMs: LG Innotek was reported as the exclusive 3D-sensor supplier for Apple Vision Pro (KED Global, 2024-02-14) while supplying ~70% of iPhone camera modules. Luxshare reportedly stopped Vision Pro production at the start of 2025 (IDC via FT). Camera-module and assembly chain. Within this file only Luxshare Precision (Xreal shareholder) and Goertek (XR reference designs at CES 2026) surface, with no documented module supply relationship to any of the six OEMs; Q Tech, CML, Optotune and Sunny have no public link either. Camera-module makers sit between poLight and the OEM ('it is the OEM… who is kind of the big boss'). SHARP mentioned poLight at a Tech-Day and is in dialogue with poLight; Tongxing hosts poLight's final-test capacity. Sunny Optical claims the global No.1 share in smart-glasses imaging modules (1H25 XR revenue RMB 1.2bn) and showed its own AI glasses at CES 2026. It is a module-level competitor/customer for any actuator supplier, with no stated actuator technology. poLight's manufacturing chain: STMicroelectronics has made the PZT thin-film actuator wafers at its 200 mm Agrate fab since the 2014 TFP launch, and Tong Hsing (THEIL) assembled TLenses from at least 2017 (400→1,000 wafers/month plan). ST is also Metalenz's metasurface foundry; no ST-Meta tunable-lens link was found. Camera-module and assembly chain around glasses: Goertek (Meta Quest/Ray-Ban/Ray-Ban Display assembler), Luxshare (Vision Pro assembly, possible Meta glasses share), Sunny Optical (smart-glasses ramp, AF cameras for AR), Cowell/Largan (Vision Pro modules) and STMicro (poLight's piezo-MEMS foundry). No teardown identifies a camera-module maker or AF actuator in any Meta glasses.

lanes.name: Meta patents & people
lanes.blurb: Meta-side patents, papers, job posts and people evidence relevant to autofocus. Includes the 2025 Reality Labs paper arguing against autofocus in all-day AI glasses (a counter-signal), a job post for passthrough camera IQ, piezo tunable-lens AF patents reportedly citing poLight, and a LinkedIn claim of a piezo tunable-lens AF module qualified for AR/VR/MR. Meta patent filings on wearable cameras with low-power autofocus (US20230280637A1, abandoned May 2025; US12493197B2, granted Dec 2025) cite CML and poLight prior art. These are examiner citations, not supply evidence, but show Meta engineering actuator-level AF for wearables. Meta holds a cluster of wearable-camera patents describing a PZT thin-film piezo tunable lens for >100° FOV cameras and a tunable-lens barrel for AR glasses. US 12,663,619 B2 (granted 2026-06-23) cites three poLight TLens documents retrieved 2022-10-19, and ex-Meta inventor Lidu Huang says he led a piezo tunable-lens AF module through AR/VR/MR reliability qualification; no Meta fab or Meta-ST deal was found. Meta Platforms Technologies' patent and people trail: a 2022–2023 cluster of piezo-membrane tunable-lens camera filings (window / polymer / glass membrane / thin-film PZT) granted Dec 2025 – Jun 2026, with US 12,663,619's IDS listing three poLight TLens documents retrieved Oct 2022. Inventor Lidu Huang's LinkedIn says the piezo AF module passed full AR/VR/MR reliability qualification before he left in Apr 2025. This is the strongest circumstantial evidence that Meta's autofocus glasses camera is TLens-adjacent. Meta's patent and people evidence: the granted wide-FOV PZT tunable-autofocus patent US 12,663,619 (citing three 2022 poLight documents), lens-barrel tunable-lens patents and the Sept 2026 continuation, plus filings citing CML and poLight, and a former engineer's LinkedIn claim of a qualified piezoelectric tunable-lens AF module. Shows R&D direction, not the production BOM.

lanes.name: Analysts, brokers & press
lanes.blurb: Market-sizing and shipment claims from Omdia, which puts Meta at 7.4m AI glasses in 2025 and 3.4m (81% share) in 1H26. These volumes set the scale of any Meta design-win for an autofocus supplier, even though the mainstream glasses remain fixed-focus. Only Analyst Group (commissioned, NOK 9.0/share) formally covers poLight. DBS covers Q Tech and cites 'low-power tunable lenses' as a smart-glasses opportunity but, in the accessible notes, never names poLight, Meta or 2027; the alleged DBS 'H1 2027' Meta/Q Tech/poLight claim remains unverified. Press and analyst commentary relevant to the SMA-vs-TLens comparison: Karl Guttag's CES 2023 power figures (CML ~64 mW moving vs TLens <6 mW), Yole's read of the Alps licence, and Everbright's sizing of the TDK→Q Tech deal. Analyst material in this file is limited to Patsnap's 2026-09-17 liquid-lens AF actuator patent landscape (LG Innotek 7, Corning 5, Meta 3, Apple 3; filings down 67% 2021-2024). Analyst, broker and press claims: DBS's Aug-2026 Q Tech note publicly cites "low-power tunable lenses" in smart glasses, while the Meta/1H27 mass-production sentence attributed to it is gated and unverified; DBS on Sunny flags an FY27 smart-glasses ramp; Counterpoint and Everbright add manufacturing-share and Cowell colour. Press and analyst claims: KGOnTech's March 2023 CES/PW report placed TLens in the Magic Leap 2 and Sharp's CES-2023 VR prototype at <6 mW, an early confirmed-in-product data point for poLight in head-worn devices. Analyst, broker, market-data and in-thread assistant claims: DBS Research (26 Aug 2026) is the only source naming a Meta + Q Tech + poLight project with 1H27 mass production; Omdia, Counterpoint and TrendForce supply market sizing; the GPT-6 Pro assistant's probability estimates, rankings and valuation models are logged here.

events.title: Earliest core TLens patents filed; expire from September 2026
events.detail: CEO on 2026-08-19: the core 2006 patents 'start to expire starting this September [2026]'; strategy has been to 'build around that patent'.

events.title: poLight priority for EP2074465B1 'Polymer lens' (Haugholt), foundational deformable-polymer IP
events.detail: poLight (then PoLight AS) priority date for EP2074465B1 'Polymer lens' by Haugholt — foundational deformable-polymer lens IP; granted 2013-06-12.

events.title: poLight priority for US8045280B2 'Compact adjustable lens' and US8883019B2 (Henriksen)
events.detail: poLight priority for US8045280B2 'Compact adjustable lens' and US8883019B2 'Method for manufacturing adjustable lens' (Henriksen); granted 2011-10-25 and 2014-11-11.

events.title: Varioptic AF liquid lenses 'deployed since 2007' (camcorders, barcode, security)
events.detail: Laser Focus World: Varioptic electrowetting AF liquid lenses deployed in consumer/industrial devices since 2007.

events.title: poLight priority for EP2115500B1 'Flexible lens assembly with variable focal length'
events.detail: poLight priority for EP2115500B1 'Flexible lens assembly with variable focal length', granted 2011-11-16.

events.title: Optotune founded as ETH Zurich spin-off (Dietikon)
events.detail: Optotune Switzerland AG founded in 2008 by Manuel Aschwanden, David Niederer and Mark Ventura as an ETH Zurich spin-off 'focusing and steering light'; electrically focus-tunable shape-changing liquid lenses with voice-coil actuators.

events.title: Optotune ranked No. 1 Swiss startup (Top100 Swiss Startup Award)
events.detail: Company about-us page lists the 2011 Top100 Swiss Startup Award ranking.

events.title: Varioptic B617 smartphone liquid lens with OIS + AF, 'up to 90% less power' than VCM
events.detail: Second-generation programmable liquid lens for smartphones with OIS and AF; 'up to 90% less power' than VCM; sampling April 2011. No smartphone design win reported.

events.title: poLight signs SVTC process-demonstration deal to scale TLens to ~1 M units/month on 8-inch wafers
events.detail: Agreement with SVTC Technologies (US) to scale TLens manufacturing: ~1 million units/month on 8-inch wafers, with parallel ramp at a larger manufacturer.

events.title: poLight priority for US9964672B2 piezo-actuator optimisation for deformable lens (Phair)
events.detail: poLight priority for US9964672B2 'Method for optimizing piezoelectric actuator structure for deformable lens' (Phair); granted 2018-05-08.

events.title: poLight priority for EP3170038B1 tunable microlens; US10,473,900 later cited in Meta's US 12,663,619
events.detail: poLight priority for EP3170038B1 'Tunable microlens with variable structure element' (Phair); the US counterpart US10,473,900 (granted 2019-11-12) is cited in Meta's US 12,663,619.

events.title: CML + Hutchinson Technology + Foxconn: first SMA OIS design wins, phones ship Sept 2014
events.detail: First design wins (May 2014) for SMA OIS actuators; phones 'reached market in September 2014'; capacity 'millions of units monthly'.

events.title: ST unveils TFP thin-film piezo MEMS process with poLight as 'one of the first customers'; Agrate 200 mm volume mid-2015
events.detail: ST TFP process launch: poLight TLens '10 times faster than VCM ... 1/20 of the power'; volume production from the 200 mm Agrate fab targeted mid-2015.

events.title: poLight ramps capacity with ST; volume production planned 2H 2015; 'could easily second source'
events.detail: eeNews (2014-2015): 'poLight is ramping up manufacturing capacity in a cooperation with ST Microelectronics ... volume production planned for the second half of 2015'; 'the company owns the full process IP and could easily second source'.

events.title: Sheba Microsystems founded (2015 per company release; 2016 per Ontario delegate page)
events.detail: Fabless Toronto MEMS company led by CEO Dr. Faez Ba-Tis and CTO Ridha Ben Mrad; founding year given as 2015 in its Jan-2024 release summary and 2016 on the Ontario CES-2026 delegate page.

events.title: poLight ramping TLens capacity with ST as manufacturing partner; volume production H2 2015
events.detail: poLight said it was "ramping up manufacturing capacity in a cooperation with ST Microelectronics as a manufacturing partner, with volume production planned for the second half of 2015"; poLight owns the process IP and "could easily second source".

events.title: TDK announces $126M purchase of Hutchinson Technology (CML's SMA partner)
events.detail: Origin of SMA know-how inside TDK's camera-actuator group; Hutchinson was CML's original SMA OIS manufacturing partner.

events.title: Alps Alpine ATMC1Z9 bi-directional AF actuator enters mass production
events.detail: VCM AF actuator mass-production announcement.

events.title: Spectacles gen 1 announced: single camera, 115° FOV circular video
events.detail: Snap announced its first Spectacles camera glasses with a single fixed-focus camera, 115° FOV, recording circular video for Snapchat.

events.title: Spectacles gen 1 released via Snapbot vending machines
events.detail: First Spectacles went on sale through Snapbot vending machines.

events.title: Invenios completes acquisition of Varioptic from Parrot Drones
events.detail: Invenios LLC closed the acquisition of Varioptic from Parrot Drones (undisclosed amount); assets moved to Invenios France SAS.

events.title: CML secures first China manufacturing licence with TDK
events.detail: Per CML's May 2024 retrospective: CML 'secured its first manufacturing license in China with TDK in 2017'.

events.title: Optotune opens first manufacturing site outside Switzerland (Trnava, Slovakia)
events.detail: First production site outside Switzerland opened in Slovakia in 2017, per the about-us page.

events.title: Stanford focus-tunable VR display research using Optotune lenses (PNAS 2017)
events.detail: PNAS 2017 'Optimizing virtual reality for all users through gaze-contingent and adaptive focus displays' (Stanford, 2016-2017) listed on Optotune's publications page; display-side use of Optotune lenses, not camera AF.

events.title: Varioptic becomes part of Corning (Varioptic + Invenios technologies)
events.detail: John Duke (Corning): 'Varioptic became a part of Corning in 2017 through an acquisition that included Varioptic and Invenios technologies.'

events.title: poLight priority for US11029511B2 'Low wavefront error piezoelectrically actuated optical element'
events.detail: poLight priority for WO2018154139A1 / US11029511B2 (Kartashov, Craen); US grant 2021-06-08; family EP3586175B1 (2023-07-19), CN110418984B, JP7377110B2, KR102577908B1.

events.title: TechInsights teardown of Spectacles: Ambarella A12, Kingston ePOP, Nordic nRF51822
events.detail: TechInsights 'Deep Dive Teardown' of Spectacles gen 1 identified Ambarella A12 camera SoC, Kingston ePOP memory and Nordic nRF51822.

events.title: NEXTLENS Switzerland AG founded (Dietikon) to bring tunable optics to mobile phones
events.detail: startup.ch: NEXTLENS 'holding company focusing on bringing innovative tunable optical components to the mobile phone industry', founded June 2017, Dietikon (startupticker gives 2019, canton NW). Same town as Optotune; corporate relationship not verified.

events.title: poLight priority for US11231528B2 (OIS+focus) and US20200204740A1 multi-camera module, latter cited by Meta
events.detail: poLight priority for US11231528B2 'Lens assembly for optical image stabilization and focus adjustment' (Craen; granted 2022-01-25) and US20200204740A1/EP3646100B1 'Module with a plurality of cameras for integration in a mobile device' (Tallaron) — the latter is cited in Meta's US 12,663,619.

events.title: poLight Q1-2017: ST makes actuator, Tong Hsing (THEIL) assembles; 400→1,000 wafers/month plan (0.9→2.25 M units/month)
events.detail: Interim report: 'poLight works primarily with two sub-contractors – STMicroelectronics (ST) and Tong Hsing Electronic Industries, Ltd. (THEIL). ST produces the actuator, and THEIL assembles the complete product.' 'A capacity increase from 400 wafers/month to 1 000 wafers/month is under planning (i.e. 900 000 to 2 250 000 units per month un-yielded) in cooperation with ST.' First design-win targeted 1H 2017.

events.title: poLight Q2-2017: ST working on further capacity increases; improved packaging at THEIL; wafers buffered for 1H 2018 delivery
events.detail: 'ST is currently working on further capacity increases'; improved TLens packaging 'underway at THEIL'; ST material used for assembly at THEIL 'for yield optimization ... and for supply to various customer qualification programs'; wafers buffered for a potential customer delivery in 1H 2018.

events.title: Optotune passes 100 employees
events.detail: About-us milestone: headcount passed 100 in 2018.

events.title: Corning Varioptic manufacturing capacity 'nearly doubled in 2018'
events.detail: Frédéric Laune (Corning): 'Our manufacturing capacity nearly doubled in 2018'; sales doubled over two years.

events.title: Spectacles 2 released; cumulative sales 220,000 pairs by May 2018
events.detail: Spectacles 2 released; cumulative sales reported at 220,000 pairs as of May 2018.

events.title: poLight priority for US11448849B2 stress-distributing support; cited by two Meta filings of 2022-01-04
events.detail: poLight priority for US11448849B2 'Optical element with stress distributing supporting structure' (pub US20210231903A1 2021-07-29; granted 2022-09-20). Its Google 'Cited By' list contains two Meta filings: US20230213729A1 and US20230213780A1 (both priority 2022-01-04).

events.title: Grethe Viksaas becomes board chair
events.detail: Board tenure listed as 'June 2018' in the 2025 annual report.

events.title: Apple priority for US10852553B2 'Electronic device with a tunable lens' (vision correction, not camera)
events.detail: Apple priority for US10852553B2 'Electronic device with a tunable lens' (granted 2020-12-01) — fluid-filled varifocal lens for vision correction in a head-mounted device, not a camera.

events.title: poLight ASA lists on Oslo Børs (ticker PLT)
events.detail: IPO on Oslo Børs on 2018-10-01.

events.title: Optotune sales office established in Taiwan
events.detail: About-us milestone: Taiwan sales office opened 2019; Optotune also lists production in Taiwan.

events.title: 2-millionth Corning Varioptic lens delivered (machine vision, barcode, medical)
events.detail: Announced at Laser World of Photonics, June 2019; markets named are machine vision, barcode and medical imaging.

events.title: Spectacles 3 announced: two HD cameras, US$380 (released Nov 2019)
events.detail: Spectacles 3 announced with two HD cameras at US$380; released November 2019.

events.title: CNBC: Facebook enlists Luxottica to co-develop AR glasses (Orion)
events.detail: CNBC reported Facebook had enlisted Ray-Ban maker Luxottica to co-develop AR glasses codenamed Orion; EssilorLuxottica later said the two have worked on wearables "since 2019".

events.title: Amazon Echo Frames 1st gen (Day 1 Edition) introduced at $179.99, audio-only
events.detail: Invitation-only first-generation Echo Frames launched at $179.99; audio-only with no camera and no display.

events.title: poLight DK201970808A1 'Rotational element for wearable device imaging' (Kilpinen)
events.detail: Earliest poLight filing explicitly titled for wearable imaging: DK201970808A1 'Rotational element for wearable device imaging' (Kilpinen).

events.title: First TLens Silver consumer product: children's smartwatch phone with AF camera
events.detail: 'A smartwatch phone for children, with a main camera with an advanced autofocus (AF) function delivered by poLight'. Brand not named by poLight (Xiaomi-ecosystem watch per user's prior research, circumstantial).

events.title: CML blog: SMA 3D-sensing doubles LiDAR range to 10 m for AR; Tier 1 samples Q3 2020
events.detail: 'Tier 1 smartphone supply chains are including this functionality in module samples planned to be available in Q3 this year.'

events.title: Facebook–Luxottica smart-glasses partnership announced at Connect 2020

events.title: Quest 2 unveiled at Facebook Connect (US$299 / US$399)
events.detail: Quest 2 announced at Facebook Connect 2020 at US$299 (64GB) / US$399 (256GB).

events.title: Barcode design-win announced (still repeat POs in Q3 2025, NOK 0.9m)
events.detail: Barcode-scanner design-win that was still generating repeat orders in Q3 2025 (NOK 0.9m).

events.title: Quest 2 ships; 4 IR tracking cameras, no colour passthrough
events.detail: Quest 2 went on sale with four infrared tracking cameras and no colour passthrough.

events.title: Echo Frames 2nd gen announced at $249.99 (shipped 2020-12-10)
events.detail: Second-generation Echo Frames announced at $249.99 and shipped 2020-12-10; still audio-only.

events.title: One-millionth Optotune component shipped
events.detail: About-us milestone: 'One-millionth Optotune component shipped' in 2021.

events.title: poLight AR2021: two Asian assembly partners; >1 M/month assembly capacity targeted by end-2022; ST processing wafer backlog
events.detail: 'Polymer and wafers with actuators are shipped to manufacturing partners in the Philippines and Taiwan'; 'poLight collaborates with two assembly partners in Asia ... events.title: 2021 decks reportedly cite ~19 AR projects, 3 design-wins expected 1H 2022
events.detail: From user's earlier research; not re-verified because 2021–2022 decks were not retrievable in the session.

events.title: Lenovo ThinkReality A3 enterprise smart glasses announced at CES 2021 (~$1,499)
events.detail: Lenovo announced ThinkReality A3 enterprise smart glasses at CES 2021, available mid-2021 at about $1,499.

events.title: poLight DK202170027A1 piezo lens with additional coatings (cf. Meta claim 4 IR-blocking coating)
events.detail: poLight DK202170027A1 'Piezoelectrically actuated optical lens with additional coatings' (Henriksen) — coating (e.g. IR-cut) integration on the tunable lens; cf. claim 4 of Meta's US 12,663,619 (IR-blocking coating on the hard substrate).

events.title: US Army awards Microsoft IVAS production agreement worth up to $21.88 billion
events.detail: The US Army awarded Microsoft a fixed-price IVAS production agreement worth up to $21.88 billion.

events.title: poLight priority for WO2022207643A1 / EP4314911B1 thermal expansion compensation (EP granted 2026-03-11)
events.detail: poLight priority for WO2022207643A1 / EP4314911B1 'Thermal expansion compensation in tunable lenses' (Craen); EP granted 2026-03-11.

events.title: Xiaomi Mi MIX Fold ships NEXTLENS liquid lens in telephoto/macro camera
events.detail: Nextlens via gophotonics: 'first ever usage of its novel liquid lens element in a flagship phone'; Xiaomi launch 'today' per Android Central (date approx. from article).

events.title: CML launches ultra-slim OIS+AF solutions for premium smartphone cameras
events.detail: Product launch press release for ultra slim OIS+AF SMA actuators.

events.title: Spectacles gen 4: first AR display, 2 RGB cameras, Snapdragon XR1, developer-only
events.detail: Fourth-generation Spectacles introduced an AR display with two RGB cameras on Snapdragon XR1; developer-only distribution.

events.title: STMicroelectronics–Metalenz metasurface optics partnership disclosed
events.detail: ST partnership with Metalenz (metasurface flat optics, not a tunable/AF lens) disclosed June 2021; context: ST is also poLight's PZT MEMS foundry.

events.title: CML launches its first SMA driver ICs
events.detail: 'Best in class driver ICs for SMA applications' — start of CML's own-silicon strategy.

events.title: CML opens Tokyo office
events.detail: Expansion into Japan with a new Tokyo office.

events.title: Ray-Ban Stories launched and on sale same day from US$299, dual 5MP cameras
events.detail: Meta/EssilorLuxottica launched Ray-Ban Stories with "dual integrated 5MP cameras" and 30 s video, from US$299 (€329), in US/AU/CA/IE/IT/UK; announcement and availability on the same day.

events.title: Chris Liu becomes Senior Director & GM of Q Tech IoT BU; later Q Tech nominee on poLight board
events.detail: Chris Liu becomes Senior Director & GM of Q Technology's IoT Business Unit ('since Oct 2021'); he is later a Q Tech-nominated member of poLight's board per the poLight Q3 2025 deck.

events.title: CML opens SF office: 'multiple commercial engagements with the US technology giants ... AR/VR'
events.detail: [Verification: partially supported — CML page quotes Osmant verbatim: 'CML now has multiple commercial engagements with the US technology giants ... smartphones and AR/VR devices'; Larry Golob, Head of Business Development for NA. Page shows no publication date, so 2021-10-18 is unverified.] Andrew Osmant, MD: 'CML now has multiple commercial engagements with the US technology giants, to implement our compact, low power actuator technology into future consumer products such as smartphones and AR/VR devices'. Head of BD North America Larry Golob. Customers anonymous.

events.title: Connect 2021: company renamed Meta; no new hardware shipped
events.detail: Facebook rebranded as Meta at Connect 2021; no new hardware was shipped from the event.

events.title: Echo Frames 2nd-gen refresh with new colours and lens options
events.detail: Refresh of the 2nd-gen Echo Frames with new colours and lens options; no hardware change in camera (none present).

events.title: CML announces ultra-slim high-precision rotary SMA actuator
events.detail: New rotary SMA actuator product announcement.

events.title: CML reaches 500 patents granted/pending
events.detail: Patent-portfolio milestone of 500 granted and pending patents.

events.title: Superlead (China machine vision) begins using TLens
events.detail: Superlead 'began using our tunable optics TLens in 2022'; by March 2025 nine Superlead products use TLens.

events.title: poLight technical paper: TLens = soft polymer, flexible glass membrane, thin-film PZT; <6 mW incl. driver
events.detail: poLight documentation describes TLens as a soft optical polymer between a flexible glass membrane and a rigid back window with a thin-film PZT actuator on the membrane; TLens Silver consumes <6 mW including driver. The prospectus describes the same construction.

events.title: poLight 48 MP / 120-degree / F2.2 TLens Add-In reference design (TTL 6.8 mm, BFL 0.73 mm)
events.detail: The wide-FOV TLens Silver Add-In reference design: 107.9-degree horizontal, 119.9-degree diagonal FOV, F/2.2, TTL 6.8 mm, BFL 0.73 mm, focus 10 cm to infinity; explicitly a reference design not yet built into an actual camera module.

events.title: Meta files US20230213729A1 low-power AF camera for smartwatch/wristband (Lidu Huang); cites poLight
events.detail: Meta priority/filing of US17/568,595 (US20230213729A1, abandoned) 'Camera device assembled with lens-to-sensor distance that reduces auto-focusing actuation power' (Lidu Huang, Peng, Xiong, Hu) — VCM/SMA-spring lens actuator for a smartwatch/wristband camera (CN family CN116405761A). Cites poLight US20210231903A1.

events.title: SPIE AR/VR/MR 2022: CML talk 'SMA actuators for AR and VR applications'
events.detail: Dr Ben Brown (Director R&D) presents; SMA 'as applicable to AR and VR camera devices as ... smartphone cameras, for which CML's technology has shipped in 10s of millions of devices'; also haptic glove.

events.title: Corning launches 2.0 refractive-index glass wafers for AR/MR waveguides
events.detail: Corning's AR effort is waveguide glass: 2.0 index wafers (150/200/300 mm) shown at SPIE AR|VR|MR and Photonics West. Not an autofocus product.

events.title: TechInsights teardown: Ray-Ban Stories cameras fixed-focus, no voice coil or magnets
events.detail: TechInsights: "The six lenses sit in a fixed focus lens barrel, with no voice coil or magnets." Establishes that Meta's first camera glasses had no autofocus actuator.

events.title: CML Chairman's statement: 22 smartphones, 16 licensees, 'active dialogue' with AR/VR corporations
events.detail: Dr M P Knight: AF+OIS actuator 'now in mass production with the first product launched in a handset in late 2021'; '16 companies now hold a licence'; 3D-sensing demonstrated 'principally on the US West Coast'; 'we are in active dialogue with major corporations focused on the AR/VR world'; funding round in preparation.

events.title: poLight presents 'New PZT MEMS Tunable Optics Technology Solutions' at MSTC 2022 (later cited by Meta patent)
events.detail: MEMS Sensor Technical Congress talk by poLight, subsequently listed under 'Other Publications' in Meta's US 12,663,619 B2.

events.title: CML and Interhaptics collaborate on haptics for the metaverse
events.detail: Haptics collaboration announcement.

events.title: Share split 1:5
events.detail: Share split 1:5 effective 2022-05-30.

Lens actuator + sensor-shift actuator for a wearable camera; cites four Cambridge Mechatronics documents (US20170219842A1, US20220106941A1, US12037991B2, US20220141357A1).

events.title: ST VL53L8 dToF sensor: first metasurface (Metalenz) optics in mass production
events.detail: Boston/Geneva release: ST VL53L8 is the first product with Metalenz metasurface optics in mass production.

events.title: Meta provisional 63/392,285: priority of 'Lens barrel with an integrated tunable lens' family (Lidu Huang)
events.detail: Meta provisional 63/392,285 — priority date of the 'Lens barrel with an integrated tunable lens' family (Lidu Huang, Brookmire, Vijay Kumar, Cotoros). events.title: Pico 4 unveiled; released 2022-10-18
