leadtimes.rationale: Meta VR Glasses, US$1,299.99, 'Available Spring 2027' (2027-03-01 to 2027-05-31), the only announced device with documented 'passthrough with autofocus and depth'. Norms used: design-in / qualification complete 12-18 months before launch; qualification orders 9-15 months before; production POs and ramp 3-6 months before; module mass production 2-4 months before (Nov 2026-Mar 2027). Program A's qualification POs of 2025-08-06, 2026-02-11 and 2026-06-18 sit 18.8, 12.6 and 8.4 months before the window start, bracketing the 9-18-month qualification and design-in bands; Q Tech's 'Ramp in 2H26/2027' (2026-08-24) and Sunny Optical's 'volume ramp-up' (2026-08-26) sit in the ramp band. No production PO has been announced as of 2026-10-06 and Meta names no supplier; VCM, Optotune and CML are listed as alternatives Meta's own patents cite.

Meta 'Artemis' consumer AR glasses, a full-year 2027 rumor window (Bloomberg/Reuters) that Bosworth 'would not commit to' on 2026-09-24, so the bands are wide. Same norms as above (12-18 / 9-15 / 3-6 months). Program C, the NOK 5m AR-camera design PO of 2025-10-13 with validation modules shipped end-Q2 2026, falls 14.6 and 6.1 months before 2027-01-01, which only fits design-in if Artemis launches late in 2027; poLight describes it as a camera 'that could be used in several AR head-worn devices', i.e. a platform. Meta's 2025-11-14 application for an LC/electrowetting 'tunable lens camera module for AR glasses' shows a non-piezo path still in research. Evidence for any supplier is thin.

Quest 4 'Griffin' gaming headset, no earlier than H2 2027 and possibly 2028 (rumor; Bosworth confirmed two devices on the roadmap on 2026-02-10). Quest 3 and 3S shipped 2x4 MP passthrough with no autofocus reported; if the VR Glasses' autofocus passthrough carries over, design-in would run Jan 2026-Dec 2027 under the 12-18-month norm. Q Tech's product map lists a 'VR VST TLens AF camera' and Luxshare is building a 9m-unit/yr Vietnam VR line tied to Meta. No direct evidence links any actuator supplier to Griffin.

Binocular Ray-Ban Display successor 'Hypernova 2', timing unresolved between H2 2026 (The Information, 2026-02-19) and 2027 (Bloomberg, 2025-04-01); not shown at Connect 2026 and Bosworth said on 2026-09-24 there is 'no new version of the hardware', so only the 2027 end of this rumor window is live. Bands follow the same 12-18 / 9-15 / 3-6-month norms. The current Display uses an OmniVision LCoS engine and a 12 MP camera with no autofocus claim; poLight's TWedge wobulation part is not expected to be mass-production ready before about 2028, so a 2027 Hypernova 2 would precede it. Evidence is thin on both display and camera actuators.

Apple N50 display-less AI glasses, shipping 'by the end of 2027' with an unveil at WWDC June 2027 (Gurman 2026-07-26, reiterated 2026-09-27); two camera sensors, one capture and one computer-vision, with no autofocus or module vendor reported. Norms as above; Kuo's Q2 2027 mass-production call would pull production POs into Q1 2027. Apple-side actuator pointers: ex-CML CTO Ben Brown at Apple from about Mar 2026, 18 months before the window; SEMCO's fine-pitch coil supply to a 'global big tech' with possible XR expansion; LG Innotek's exclusive Vision Pro 3D-sensor role. Q Tech has no meaningful Apple exposure and poLight has never referred to Apple; Apple's own tunable-lens patents are prescription see-through lenses, not camera AF.

Samsung/Google intelligent eyewear SM-O200P (Warby Parker) / SM-O200J (Gentle Monster), November 2026 per a Samsung official (2026-10-01); FCC filing shows a single 12 MP camera on Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1. Autofocus is claimed only by VRARA 'early reports' (2026-02-09). Under the 12-18 / 9-15 / 3-6-month norms, design-in should have completed by Nov 2025 and production POs by Aug 2026. Program B's stream fits those bands loosely: the PoC PO of 2025-11-24 sits in the qualification band, the mass-production follow-ons of 2026-04-07 and 2026-05-20 and the 2026-07-10 design-in sit in the production-PO band, and Q4 2026 deliveries run 1-2 months later than the 2-4-month module-MP norm, which is compatible with a November launch only if the first build is small; Q Tech reported 'small-batch deliveries for 2 leading overseas terminal clients' at year-end 2025. Samsung's in-house actuator and module chain (SEMCO) is the default assumption; nothing names poLight or Q Tech.

Android XR in-lens display glasses in 2027, stated by Google at I/O 2026; Samsung's colour-display version 'may launch late 2027' and Kering's Gucci glasses 'probably 2027' sit inside the same window. Full-year window, so bands are wide under the 12-18 / 9-15 / 3-6-month norms. Supplier-side signals that fit a 2027-2028 display device are TWedge sample orders from 'a leading AR platform company' (2026-03-07) and from a 'leading consumer OEM' (2026-09-21), but poLight itself says a mass-production-ready TWedge 'could be needed in two years' from Feb 2026, i.e. 2028. Camera autofocus for these glasses is unreported.

Snap Specs, US$2,195, shipping 'later this fall' 2026 in the US, UK and France; two RGB and two IR cameras with no megapixel or focus-type specification published as of 2026-10-06; initial run reportedly capped at about 100,000 units. Norms as above put design-in in Apr-Dec 2025 and production POs in Apr-Sep 2026. poLight's Program B design-in on 2026-07-10 with Q4 2026 deliveries is 83 days before the window opens, late for a first build unless camera modules are assembled in Q3-Q4; Snap is a U.S. company but poLight labels Program B a 'leading consumer OEM' rather than 'top tier U.S.'. No supplier evidence names Snap.

Xreal Aura, fall 2026 in the US, UK, Japan, Canada and South Korea at no more than US$1,500; two world-facing tracking cameras plus one high-resolution camera with undisclosed focus type. Xreal's 2025 Eye module was explicitly fixed focus, 'autofocus not supported', and Xreal ships only 125-137k units a year, so volumes would be small. Norms as above; Program B's 2026-07-10 design-in is only 53 days before the window start, which argues against Aura unless it slips into Q4. Nothing in the supplier lanes names Xreal; Alibaba and Luxshare are shareholders.

Alibaba Qwen N1 / N1 Pro glasses with a 50 MP camera, pre-orders 2026-09-22, in-stock sale 2026-10-13, China only. All three phases are already in the past under the norms; a 50 MP sensor implies a larger lens stack where any autofocus would more likely be a VCM-class actuator from the smartphone chain than a 3 mm-aperture tunable lens. The only Alibaba-ecosystem TLens link is Ant Group's 'Look to Pay' demo glasses with a TLens camera on 2026-08-06. No supplier evidence for N1 itself.

Inferred next-generation Qwen glasses in 2027, based only on Alibaba's 4-6-month release cadence (preview 2025-07-28, launch 2025-11-27, Qwen Glasses 2026-03-03, N1 2026-09-10) with March (MWC) and September (Apsara) as recurring slots. Bands follow the generic norms across a full-year window. Ant Group's TLens demo of 2026-08-06 would sit 5-17 months before a 2027 device, inside the qualification band, but it is a demo, not an order. Evidence is thin and the window itself is unannounced.

Amazon consumer 'Jayhawk' camera-plus-monocular-display glasses, reported by The Information on 2025-09-10 for 'late 2026 or early 2027' with no follow-up reporting in the 391 days since, suggesting slippage. Bands follow the norms. Amazon's AR patents linked to Jayhawk cover UI and fulfilment, not optics or autofocus, and its only shipping glasses are driver units with 'integrated cameras' scaling to 20,000-plus devices by end-2027, a volume too small to show in any supplier's accounts. No supplier signal points at Amazon.

Pico Space Pro, Q4 2026 (China first) after the 2026-09-02 debut event was cancelled on 2026-08-25; a social leak claims the first week of October at US$2,899. Q Tech named PICO among the AR brands it covers in its FY2023 deck and lists a 'VR VST TLens AF camera' on its product map, so Pico is the most plausible non-Meta host for that line. Under the norms, production POs should already have been placed (Apr-Sep 2026); poLight's Program B ('leading consumer OEM', design-in 2026-07-10, Q4 deliveries) would fit this window on timing, though poLight describes that customer as 'a major player in the ecosystem'. No teardown yet.

Viture Helix enterprise AI safety glasses on NVIDIA XR AI, 12 MP camera, from US$600, shipping Q1 2027; focus type unstated. Bands follow the norms. poLight's enterprise cadence (repeat MR head-mounted design-win with an initial mass-production PO of ~NOK 0.4m on 2025-10-09; IRIS-scanner design-in 2025-10-20) is the type of signal that would fit a Q1 2027 enterprise device, but nothing names Viture, and Viture is being sued by Xreal. Thin.

Xiaomi AI Glasses second generation, rumoured on 2026-08-05 to be 'R&D complete' but paused and possibly slipping to Q4 2026 or 2027; Xiaomi called the report false. Generation one (2025-06-26) used a 12 MP Sony IMX681 with Goertek as ODM. Xiaomi was poLight's first consumer TLens customer (Mitu watch, 2020-01-07) and used a NEXTLENS liquid lens in the Mi MIX Fold (2021-03-30), so it has a history of adopting tunable optics, but there is no signal for gen 2. Bands follow the norms over a rumor window.

matches.title: Program A qualification PO #1 (Aug 2025) vs Meta VR Glasses spring 2027
matches.comment: The first Program A PO (2025-08-06, ~NOK 1.7m, 50% firm) sits 18.8-21.8 months before the Mar-May 2027 window, at the front edge of the 12-18-month design-in norm, which is what a qualification programme that must close by mid-2026 for a spring-2027 build would look like; poLight's Q2-2025 report added that the OEM 'has moved forward with programmes to prepare for the use of TLens'. It would be contradicted by the Q4-2026 report (2027-02-24) still calling Program A 'qualification', by no production PO appearing in the Sep 2026-Feb 2027 band, or by a VR Glasses teardown showing a non-piezo actuator.

matches.title: Program A PO #3 (Jun 2026) lands 8.4-11.4 months before spring 2027
matches.comment: PO #3 (NOK 0.7m, 2026-06-18, deliveries 'likely second half of 2026') is 256-347 days before the window; the spacing of the three POs, 189 then 127 days, is accelerating rather than fading, and a final qualification delivery 6-9 months before launch is where the 9-15-month norm puts it. Against this, the CEO still cites 'several milestones to pass', leaves ramp timing 'to be seen', and says the Q Tech line is not sized for the OEM's volume. A Q3-2026 report (2026-10-29) without Program A progress, or Program A deliveries slipping into 2027, would break the fit.

matches.title: Q Tech 'Overseas Key Customers: Ramp in 2H26/2027' vs the 3-6-month ramp band
matches.comment: Published 2026-08-24, 187 days before the window; '2H26/2027' straddles a late-2026 glasses launch (Program B) and a spring-2027 device, and 'TLens + AR Mono Engine: Volume Delivery Achieved' is the first volume wording, 161 days after 'small-batch deliveries' on 2026-03-16. The customer is unnamed and 'overseas' could equally mean Samsung, Google or Snap; Q Tech also now owns TDK's VCM/SMA actuator business, so a ramp need not be TLens. If Q Tech's FY2026 deck (Mar 2027) pushes the ramp to 2H27 or drops TLens from the roadmap, the match fails.

matches.title: 'US M brand' vendor code (Aug 2024) to the VR Glasses announcement 25 months later
matches.comment: Q Tech's H1-2024 deck (2024-08-12) said it had 'obtained US M brand vendor code' with a design-win target 'within this year'; the poLight investment 'backed by a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer' followed 246 days later and Connect 2026 came 772 days later, with the spring-2027 window 30.6 months out, a plausible new-platform camera cycle. 'M' is never expanded in any deck, and Q Tech also names PICO and HTC as XR customers. The forum claim that Q Tech supplies Meta Quest tracking and passthrough modules has no primary source; if that business is VST modules only with the AF lens sourced elsewhere, the vendor code says nothing about TLens.

matches.title: 'VR VST TLens AF camera' on Q Tech's product map 18.6 months before the only VR device announced with autofocus passthrough
matches.comment: The H1-2025 deck (2025-08-11) lists 'VR VST TLens AF camera' and 'AR SWIS TLens AF camera' and the roadmap entry '2026: TLens'; 408 days later Meta's developer page documents 'passthrough with autofocus and depth', and the 18.6-month lead to 2027-03-01 is at the top of the design-in norm. Pico Space Pro (Q4 2026) and future Galaxy XR units are alternative VST hosts, and Q Tech's 2024 deck named PICO and HTC as customers. A Space Pro teardown showing a TLens would re-attribute the line; a VR Glasses teardown showing another actuator would kill it.

matches.title: Ex-Meta engineer: piezo tunable-lens AF module passed AR/VR/MR reliability qualification by Apr 2025
matches.comment: Lidu Huang's Meta tenure (Sep 2020-Apr 2025) ends 22 months before the window and 16.8 months before the announcement; a module 'passing full reliability qualifications for AR/VR/MR' by then matches poLight's account that the OEM had qualified TLens 'for many years' and 'triggered' the Q Tech deal. The profile never says whose lens: Meta's own filings describe a window/polymer/glass-membrane/piezo stack that could be built by another MEMS line. If the module was the wristband-camera family Meta abandoned on 2025-05-08, or if no poLight production PO appears by Q1 2027, the inference weakens.

matches.title: US 12,663,619 (granted 2026-06-23): wide-FOV tunable-lens assembly citing three poLight documents
matches.comment: Meta's side retrieved poLight's TLens Add-In and Packaged TLens pages on 2022-10-19, 1,343 days before this grant, and the example design (107 deg FOV, F/2.2, TTL 5.0 mm, PZT thin film) is a passthrough-class camera; the grant arrives 8 months before the launch window. Citations prove awareness, not purchase, and the lens-barrel grant US 12,631,847 (2026-05-19) could mean Meta integrates a bought TLens or its own membrane lens. The clean contradiction would be a VR Glasses teardown naming a different lens maker, or poLight ending 2027 with no production PO.

matches.title: Meta's own paper against autofocus in all-day glasses vs Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 (fixed focus line)
matches.comment: Reality Labs' 2025-04-17 paper says autofocus actuators 'add size and weight... and require more power' and favours fixed focus for always-on glasses; Gen 2 reviews of 2025-12-11 confirmed 'simple fixed focus' and Gen 3 (2026-09-23, 12 MP, 3K, same-day ship) makes no autofocus claim. This is a negative match: it caps TLens's 2027 Meta opportunity at the puck-powered VR Glasses rather than the 7-10m-unit Ray-Ban line. A Gen 3 teardown finding an actuator would overturn it.

matches.title: Meta's Nov-2025 LC/electrowetting AR-glasses tunable-lens application vs Artemis 2027
matches.comment: Filed 2025-11-14, 13.6 months before 2027-01-01, this application describes a non-piezo tunable-lens camera module for AR glasses while Meta's latest piezo priority dates from 2023-08-28; it suggests the AR-glasses camera is still being explored, consistent with Bosworth's refusal to commit to 2027. Negative for a piezo/TLens AR-glasses win in 2027. It would be contradicted if Program C is converted into a dated AR design-in in the Q3 or Q4 2026 reports.

matches.title: Program B design-in (2026-07-10, Q4 deliveries) vs Samsung/Google glasses in November 2026
matches.comment: The design-in declaration is 114 days before 2026-11-01, inside the 3-6-month production-PO band, and the PO stream of NOK 0.9m, 2.4m, 0.8m and 0.8m (2025-11-24 to 2026-07-10, 228 days) is described as 'all for mass production'; VRARA 'early reports' of a 12 MP camera with autofocus and poLight's switch from 'top tier U.S.' to 'leading consumer OEM' both fit a Korean 'major player in the ecosystem'. Samsung normally sources camera actuators from SEMCO and the FCC filing shows a single 12 MP camera with no focus data; a November teardown showing fixed focus, or deliveries that do not step up to monthly call-offs in Q4, would contradict it.

matches.title: Program B vs Snap Specs (US$2,195, fall 2026)
matches.comment: The design-in is 83 days before the 2026-10-01 window; 'probably high-end' suits a US$2,195 product, Specs' four cameras have no published focus spec, and an initial run near 100,000 units is roughly the scale NOK ~4m of mass-production lens POs at about US$2 per lens would cover. Against it, Snap is a U.S. company and poLight reserves 'top tier U.S.' for Programs A and C, and first Specs deliveries in October leave little room for Q4 lens deliveries. A Specs teardown with fixed-focus RGB cameras would settle it.

matches.title: Program B vs Xreal Aura (fall 2026, one high-resolution camera)
matches.comment: Only 53 days separate the design-in from the 2026-09-01 window start, too short for a first build under any norm; Aura's camera focus is undisclosed, Xreal's own Eye module was fixed focus with 'autofocus not supported', and Xreal sells 125-137k units a year, modest for a 'major player in the ecosystem'. The match survives only if Aura slips into Q4 2026 and a teardown shows a piezo lens; an on-time September launch with fixed focus contradicts it.

matches.title: Q Tech 'small-batch deliveries for 2 leading overseas terminal clients' (YE2025) vs a November-2026 launch
matches.comment: Small batches at year-end 2025 are 10-11 months before November 2026, the qualification-order band, and by 2026-08-24 the deck reads 'Deliveries to 2 Top Overseas OEMs' with 'Volume Delivery Achieved', the step a pre-launch ramp would show. Samsung's group companies are its natural module source, so Q Tech's two OEMs may instead be Meta and Google or Snap; nothing in the decks names a customer. Identification of the two OEMs as non-Samsung, or Samsung's glasses proving fixed focus, would contradict it.

matches.title: Program C NOK 5m AR-camera design PO (Oct 2025) vs 2027 AR glasses
matches.comment: The design PO is 14.6 months before 2027-01-01 and the validation modules shipped end-Q2 2026 are 6.1 months before, which only fits a design-in for a product late in 2027; poLight's wording, a camera 'that could be used in several AR head-worn devices' and a possible 'platform for other customers', reads as 2028-class platform work, and TWedge is not expected to be mass-production ready before 2028. 'More visibility' is promised towards end-2026. Conversion of Program C into a dated design-in in the Q3 or Q4 2026 report would strengthen it; silence through 2027 would confirm the platform reading.

matches.title: CML CTO Ben Brown moves to Apple (Mar 2026), 18 months before N50 shipments
matches.comment: The departure (Dec 2022-Mar 2026 tenure, LinkedIn headline now 'Apple') is about 18-21 months before the Oct-Dec 2027 window, the design-in edge of the norm, and Apple already files tunable-lens patents with ex-CML CTO Richard Topliss as inventor. Those Apple filings are see-through prescription lenses, not camera autofocus, and N50's two cameras are reported without autofocus; the profile itself could not be retrieved. If Brown's Apple role is display or prescription optics, or N50 ships fixed focus, the link is irrelevant to camera actuators.

matches.title: CML's 2021 'US technology giants... AR/VR' engagements vs Vision Pro (shipped 2024-02-02)
matches.comment: 837 days separate the SF-office statement (2021-10-18) from Vision Pro shipping, a textbook design-in-to-launch span, yet iFixit's teardown identified no actuator or module supplier and CML's XR messaging went silent after 2025-05-12 (512 days). Meta's wearable-camera filing that cited CML was allowed and then abandoned. Treated as a negative or unresolved match; a Vision Pro M5 teardown identifying SMA actuators would reverse it.

matches.title: CML 'commercial projects with several industry leaders' (Jan 2023) vs Meta VR Glasses
matches.comment: Forty-four months after CML's SPIE 2023 claim, no CML-SMA XR product has surfaced; Meta's CML-citing two-stage wearable camera application was abandoned 834 days later (2025-05-08) and CML has been absent from SPIE AR/VR/MR 2025 and 2026. CML now pitches SMA for moving display optics, which could coexist with a piezo camera lens rather than compete. Negative for a camera-AF role; a VR Glasses teardown with SMA wires in the passthrough modules would contradict it.

matches.title: Optotune EL-3.1-10.8 launch (2026-09-21) vs spring 2027
matches.comment: The public launch is 161 days before the window, too late for a design-in, but the part's handling instructions existed on 2025-09-17, 17.4 months before, inside the norm; at 1.72 mm, 0.3 g and 20 mW at 10 dpt it is glasses-class, though about three times TLens's stated <6 mW, and Meta's EP search cited Optotune liquid-lens art. Optotune's own CCM page positions it for phones, action cams and robotics and no consumer customer is named. If Optotune's 2027 references stay industrial, this is a competitive-threat marker, not a match.

matches.title: Optotune's glasses-class liquid lens documented Sep 2025, 24 months before Apple N50
matches.comment: The 2025-09-17 handling document is 744 days before the Oct-Dec 2027 window, a full qualification cycle; Apple holds three liquid-lens AF patents in the Patsnap landscape and Corning (Varioptic's owner) is an Apple glass supplier. Nothing reports autofocus in N50's two cameras and nothing links Optotune to Apple, so this is a weak placeholder; Gurman's reports continuing to describe fixed cameras, or Optotune naming only industrial customers, keeps it at zero.

matches.title: SEMCO fine-pitch coils for a 'global big tech' AF/OIS actuator, XR expansion possible (Dec 2025)
matches.comment: Reported 2025-12-17, 21.5 months before late 2027; the customer profile (hundreds of millions of smartphones a year, notebooks, tablets, wearables) is Apple, and coils imply VCM or OIS-class actuators, so if N50's capture camera has autofocus the incumbent coil chain is the likelier source than a tunable lens. Negative for TLens at Apple. It would be contradicted by N50 shipping fixed focus (the current reporting) or by the XR option never materialising.

matches.title: Phoenix supply-chain preview: Goertek assembly, Sony sensors, Sunny Optical camera modules
matches.comment: Published 2026-09-20, 162 days before the window, it names the module maker and sensor vendor for Phoenix/VR Glasses but not the autofocus actuator; Sunny's H1-2026 line 'Compact High-Res AF for AR' and 'SG have entered the volume ramp-up phase' (2026-08-26) and DBS's 'FY27 ramp of major smart-glasses programmes' all sit in the 2-6-month ramp band. If Sunny builds the passthrough modules, TLens would ship as a component into Sunny, consistent with poLight's Q Tech line being 'not sized for OEM volume'. Sunny's AF module turning out VCM-based would contradict it.

matches.title: Unverified DBS sentence: Meta + Q Tech + poLight mass production 1H27
matches.comment: Mass production in 1H27 is 2-4 months before a Mar-May 2027 launch, exactly the module-MP norm, which is why the sentence is plausible; but it is a second-hand quote from a gated 2026-08-26 PDF, absent from DBS's public summary and from DBS's own Meta note of 2026-05-08, and poLight has never named Meta. It becomes evidence only if the PDF surfaces or poLight announces a production PO in the Sep 2026-Feb 2027 band; DBS's FY27 Q Tech estimates excluding a tunable-lens line would contradict it.

matches.title: First consumer TLens: Xiaomi Mitu children's watch (2020-01-07)
matches.comment: poLight's first consumer product and Xiaomi's launch coincide in January 2020; the customer was named by the press, not by poLight, and 37.8 months then passed before the next XR-relevant proof (Magic Leap 2 teardown). It shows both poLight's disclosure pattern and how slowly XR adoption has followed early wins. Nothing contradicts it.

matches.title: SnkeXR medical AR design win named on the same day (2025-10-31)
matches.comment: poLight's second disclosed AR design win was named by both sides on 2025-10-31, showing poLight does name customers when permitted; the consumer programmes' anonymity is therefore the customer's choice. Enterprise and medical scale only; nothing contradicts it.

matches.title: Sheba MEMS sensor-shift AF camera for AR/VR/XR (Jan 2024): no customer in 33 months
matches.comment: Launched 2024-01-09 with <10 mW and <5 ms claims, 1,001 days later Sheba reports 17 staff and USD 400K annual sales and a Teledyne MEMS production partner for automotive ADAS, not XR. Negative match: not a credible 2027 top-tier supplier. A named XR design-in would contradict it.

matches.title: Corning Varioptic remains an industrial liquid-lens line (Sep 2026)
matches.comment: Corning's 2026-09-24 page frames Varioptic as 'adjustable lens solutions for industrial applications' and its Oct 2026-May 2027 show calendar is all machine vision; Corning's XR presence is waveguide glass, and Meta's examiner cited Varioptic as prior art only. Negative for a Varioptic role in any 2027 consumer glasses, Apple included. A Corning consumer liquid-lens announcement would contradict it.

matches.title: TDK actuator business to Q Tech (framework Apr 2025, closed by Jun 2026): Q Tech can offer VCM, SMA or TLens
matches.comment: The framework came 13 days after the poLight investment and completion 399 days later, so for the 2H26/2027 ramp Q Tech can supply either actuator type; this cuts both ways for poLight. What to watch instead are poLight's Q Tech NRE invoices (USD 313,141 in Mar 2026, USD 178,662 in Q2 2026) and whether MEMS wafer orders resume: none were placed in 2025 or H1 2026 because inventory covers 'several millions' of lenses, so wafer orders will not lead a first ramp. A Q Tech VCM/SMA module in the VR Glasses would contradict a TLens reading.

matches.title: TWedge samples for 'a leading AR platform company' (Mar 2026) vs 2027 display glasses
matches.comment: The 2026-03-07 sample order is 10-22 months before a 2027 display device, but TWedge is an LCoS wobulation display part and poLight itself says a mass-production-ready TWedge 'could be needed in two years' from Feb 2026, i.e. 2028; so this is a 2028-class signal. Google, Samsung, Snap and Meta are all plausible 'platform' companies; the 2026-09-21 follow-on (NOK 1.2m) came from a 'leading consumer OEM'. TWedge appearing in any 2027 product would contradict the 2028 reading.

segments.title: IP and foundry foundations
segments.text: Founded in Horten in 2005, with the core TLens patent priorities from 2006-09-21 (expiring from September 2026) and the Meta-cited filings of 2014-07-18 and 2017-06-30. ST became the thin-film piezo partner in 2014-09 with 'volume production H2 2015', after an SVTC deal in 2011 that already targeted ~1M units/month; the 2017 plan was 400 to 1,000 wafers/month (0.9 to 2.25M lenses/month). The Oslo listing came on 2018-10-01. Capacity ambitions ran a decade ahead of any consumer volume.

segments.title: First wins, slow XR
segments.text: The Xiaomi Mitu watch shipped the first consumer TLens in January 2020, a barcode design-win followed on 2020-09-18 and 2021 decks cited ~19 AR projects with three design-wins expected in 1H 2022. The Magic Leap 2 teardown (2023-03-02) and Vuzix Shield (2024-04-08) were the only XR wins made public, both enterprise. FY2024 revenue was NOK 9.6m with cash of NOK 166.8m and TLens in 28 products; the first TWedge sample PO (~NOK 500k, 2024-11-21) from a 'top-tier consumer OEM' opened the current chapter.

segments.title: Q Tech alliance and Program A
segments.text: Q Tech bought 32.97% at NOK 2.69 (NOK 171.5m) on 2025-04-15, a deal management said one long-standing top-tier U.S. OEM 'triggered'. Program A qualification POs followed on 2025-08-06 (~NOK 1.7m, 50% firm), 2026-02-11 (final 50%, 189 days later) and 2026-06-18 (NOK 0.7m, 127 days later) with deliveries 'likely second half of 2026' and 'still several milestones to pass'. Cash rose from NOK 135.8m (Q1 2025) to NOK 298.2m (Q3 2025) and the share price from 6.21 to 9.75 across the two 2026 announcements; no new MEMS wafers were ordered in 2025 because inventory covers several million lenses.

segments.title: Program B from PoC to design-in
segments.text: A 'leading consumer OEM' placed POs of NOK 0.9m (2025-11-24, 'mature proof-of-concept'), 2.4m (2026-04-07, 134 days later), 0.8m (2026-05-20, 43 days) and 0.8m (2026-07-10, 51 days), NOK 4.9m in 228 days, and on the fourth PO poLight declared its first consumer AR|MR design-in with the product 'expected to launch in 2026' and deliveries in Q4 2026. Wording moved from 'promising sign' to 'not without its challenges and risks' to 'mass production POs'. AR|MR reached 86% of Q2 2026 revenue and H1 2026 revenue (NOK 20.6m) exceeded all of FY2025 (NOK 20.5m); the pipeline shows 6 design-wins and 0 design-ins in AR/MR as of Q1 2026, before this relabel.

segments.title: Watch window
segments.text: On the Q2 call (2026-08-06) the CEO said the design-in customer is separate from the Q Tech-backed OEM ('but there are more'); the earlier ChatGPT thread also read a post-quarter Q&A as separating the third programme, a document the fact-check could not locate, priced consumer TLens at ~US$2+, and said assembly and test capacity would double by end-2026. Insiders sold 1,109,586 shares at NOK 12.13 on 2026-08-27; the stock closed at NOK 14.90 on 2026-09-25 (~NOK 3.2bn market cap). Program C modules shipped for validation at end-Q2 2026 and 'more visibility' on Programs A and C is promised towards year-end. The Q3 report (2026-10-29), the Capital Markets Day (2026-10-30) and the Q4 report (2027-02-24, five days before the VR Glasses window) are the dated checkpoints; the 3-6-month production-PO band for a spring-2027 device runs Sep 2026-Feb 2027 and nothing has been announced in it as of 2026-10-06.

segments.title: Vendor code to alliance
segments.text: Chris Liu took over the IoT business unit in October 2021. The FY2023 deck (2024-03-25) reported a 'vendor code of major US customer'; 140 days later the H1-2024 deck named it 'US M brand' with a design-win target 'within this year'. The FY2024 deck (2025-03-18) said Q Tech was 'qualified as the supplier for multiple international leading manufacturers' of VR/AR/AI glasses; 28 days later it invested NOK 171.5m in poLight 'backed by a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer', and 13 days after that signed the framework to buy TDK's camera-actuator business, including SMA routes and a Philippines plant.

segments.title: Line build and roadmap
segments.text: The HKEX note of 2025-06-09 called poLight's piezo actuator 'the best solution for XR optical modules'. The H1-2025 deck (2025-08-11) put 'VR VST TLens AF camera' and 'AR SWIS TLens AF camera' on the product map with a '2026: Light Engine, TLens, TWedge, AR DSA' roadmap. By Q3 2025 the dedicated TLens line had 'all equipment installed' with capacity comparable to the Philippines line; poLight invoiced USD 313,141 of 2025 NRE in March 2026 for 'getting it qualified for mass production'. The FY2025 deck (2026-03-16) reported 'small-batch deliveries for 2 leading overseas terminal clients', 10 brands, and the TDK closing 'well underway' (completed around 2026-03-31).

segments.title: Volume wording
segments.text: The annual report (2026-04-24) showed a 29.96% poLight stake and a RMB 15.1m share of loss. The H1-2026 deck (2026-08-24) moved to 'TLens + AR Mono Engine: Volume Delivery Achieved', 'Deliveries to 2 Top Overseas OEMs', '22 Partners (+4)' and 'Overseas Key Customers: Ramp in 2H26 / 2027', 161 days after 'small-batch'; group revenue was RMB 9.92bn (+12.4%) with R&D up 24.2% to RMB 346.7m focused on AI/AR glasses. DBS initiated BUY (TP HKD 12.60) on 2026-08-26 citing 'low-power tunable lenses'. A Xueqiu post tying Q Tech's modules to Meta Quest (2026-09-22) has no primary source; the IR head bought 218,000 shares with a one-year lock on 2026-10-05.

segments.title: Smartphone-scale SMA
segments.text: Incorporated 1995-06-21; first SMA OIS design wins with Hutchinson and Foxconn shipped in September 2014; a TDK manufacturing licence followed in 2017 (TDK had bought Hutchinson for US$126m in 2015). 2021 brought ultra-slim OIS+AF (2021-04-21), first driver ICs (2021-07-02) and a Tokyo office. Everything shipped was smartphone volume, tens of millions of units.

segments.title: XR push
segments.text: The San Francisco office opening (2021-10-18) claimed 'multiple commercial engagements with the US technology giants... AR/VR devices'; SPIE AR/VR/MR talks followed on 2022-01-20, 2023-01-25 ('already engaged in commercial projects with several industry leaders') and 2024-01-29, with a CES 2023 showcase of zero-hold-power focus for displays and cameras. Patents climbed from 500 (2021-12-22) to 700 (2024-02-09) and the US$40m round closed 2024-02-13 with Intel Capital and Sony. Meta's 2022-05-31 wearable-camera filing cited four CML documents, the only producer trace of these engagements.

segments.title: Pivot and silence
segments.text: Two XR patent priorities (2024-03-04 and 2024-10-24) describe SMA-driven deformable or liquid lenses 'for glasses and... VR/AR headsets' (published 2025-09-12 and 2026-04-30), but CML was absent from SPIE 2025 and 2026 and its last XR-facing article is dated 2025-05-12, 512 days ago. A new CEO arrived 2025-04-10, Meta abandoned its CML-citing application on 2025-05-08, and CTO Ben Brown's tenure ended in March 2026 with his headline now 'Apple'. Share allotments on 2024-06-26, 2024-09-26, 2026-04-08 and 2026-06-01 suggest rolling equity raises; the live 'AI Vision Product Manager' ad cites 'AI glasses' and ~850 patents, so the ambition persists without a named XR customer.

segments.title: Industrial liquid-lens leader
segments.text: ETH spin-off founded 2008; Slovakia plant 2017; 100 employees 2018; one-millionth component 2021. The December 2022 brochure listed 250 employees, >300k units/yr cleanroom capacity and AR/VR as a market, while the EL-3-10 datasheet (revisions 2020-12-01 and 2023-03-14) remained a 3 mm industrial part. Stanford's 2017 focus-tunable VR display work used Optotune lenses, the lane's only XR research trace.

segments.title: A glasses-class part surfaces
segments.text: Eyewear-specific patents were filed 2023-08-30 (non-circular ring-actuated lens) and 2024-06-24 (gravity-coma compensation for smart glasses). The EL-3.1-10.8 handling instructions carry a 2025-09-17 date, a US Sales Manager for 'industrial and consumer applications' was posted 2026-01-08, and the datasheet (2026-09-18: 1.72 mm high, 0.3 g, 3.1 mm aperture, 20 mW at 10 dpt, 1 ms response) preceded the LinkedIn launch on 2026-09-21, 369 days after the handling document and two days before Connect 2026. Headcount is now 180+ (from 250) with 2+ million units shipped; no customer is named and the CCM page lists phones, action cams and robotics.

segments.title: Pioneer, then Corning
segments.text: Liquid autofocus lenses deployed since 2007 and a smartphone OIS+AF lens (B617, 2011-01-24, 'up to 90% less power' than VCM) never reached phone volume; Parrot sold Varioptic to Invenios (2016-12-29) and Corning absorbed it in 2017, nearly doubling capacity in 2018 and delivering the 2-millionth lens by June 2019, all to machine vision, barcode and medical.

segments.title: Industrial only
segments.text: Corning's XR presence is high-index waveguide glass (2022-01-28, 2023-12-19) with no liquid-lens mention; the Varioptic page of 2026-09-24 reads 'adjustable lens solutions for industrial applications' and the Oct 2026-May 2027 show calendar (VISION Stuttgart, ITE, Photonics West, Vision China, Automate) contains no consumer or XR event. Meta's lens-barrel examiner cited Varioptic as prior art only. Seven-plus years without a consumer signal.

segments.title: Launches without customers
segments.text: Founded 2015 (or 2016), Sheba launched an athermalising MEMS AF actuator on 2023-09-21, a sensor-shift AF camera 'for AR/VR/XR headsets' (<10 mW, <5 ms) on 2024-01-09, and the Sharp-7 automotive AF camera on 2024-05-16 with a DXOMARK report on 2024-10-10; no XR customer has been named in any release.

segments.title: Scale check
segments.text: The CES 2026 Ontario delegation listed 17 staff and USD 400K annual sales (2026-01-06); a COO was appointed 2026-06-09 and Teledyne named as MEMS production partner for ADAS actuators on 2026-06-25. 1,001 days after the XR camera launch the company remains an automotive-leaning start-up, not a candidate for a 2027 top-tier programme.

segments.title: Incumbents
segments.text: MinebeaMitsumi has built VCM/OIS actuators in Cebu since 2005 and Alps Alpine's bi-directional AF actuator entered mass production 2016-01-19; TDK bought Hutchinson (CML's SMA partner) in 2015-11. Alps started SMA actuator mass production on 2023-01-10 (30 um wire, ~40% smaller than VCM) and sampled a piezo zoom actuator on 2023-01-24, showing the incumbents already own alternatives to piezo membranes.

segments.title: Consolidation into Q Tech's orbit
segments.text: TDK's framework to sell its camera-actuator business to Q Tech's controlling shareholder (2025-04-28) led to the Actutek carve-out (2025-11-14, 200 days later), effectiveness on 2026-01-01 and completed transfer by 2026-06-01 (399 days); Everbright counted 2,000+ patents and 2,000+ employees. LG Innotek held >50% of iPhone 17 folded-zoom OIS (2025-10-01) and SEMCO neared a fine-pitch-coil supply to a 'global big tech' with 'potential expansion to XR devices' (2025-12-17). Alps showed no XR actuator at CES 2026; Mitsumi appears among Meta's VCM patent references (2026-09-26). The coil chain remains the default for any Apple or Samsung camera.

segments.title: ST and Tong Hsing backbone
segments.text: ST unveiled its thin-film piezo process on 2014-09-23 with poLight as 'one of the first customers' and Agrate 200 mm volume for mid-2015; by Q1 2017 ST made the actuator and Tong Hsing assembled, with a 400 to 1,000 wafers/month plan (0.9 to 2.25M units/month) and wafers buffered for 1H 2018 delivery. That buffered inventory is why no new wafers were needed in 2025-2026.

segments.title: Meta and Apple assembly chains
segments.text: ST-Metalenz metasurface optics went from partnership (2021-06) to a 300 mm fab licence with >140M units shipped (2025-07-10). Luxshare was the sole Vision Pro contract manufacturer (2023-07-03) and LG Innotek its exclusive 3D-sensor supplier (2024-02-14); Sunny Optical and Goertek were named Quest 3 beneficiaries (2023-09-29), Goertek committed US$280m to Vietnam (2024) and built Hypernova (2025-09-16), with the Display's camera drawing 1.0-1.7 W (2025-10-30). Sunny's 1H25 XR revenue was RMB 1,201.2m (+21.1%) as 'global NO.1' in smart-glasses imaging modules, actuator technology unstated.

segments.title: 2026 ramp signals
segments.text: Luxshare announced a US$520m, 9m-unit/yr Vietnam VR line tied to Meta (2026-01-05); ChinaTalk mapped Goertek assembly and Sunny camera modules for Ray-Ban Meta/Display with the Chinese BOM share cut from ~61% to 33.5% (2026-01-07); Counterpoint saw Goertek's share nearly doubling (2026-05-19). Sunny's H1-2026 results (2026-08-26) said smart glasses 'have entered the volume ramp-up phase' and introduced a 'Compact High-Res AF for AR'; DBS (2026-08-28) made the 'FY27 ramp of major smart-glasses programmes' its catalyst; the 2026-09-20 Phoenix preview named Goertek assembly, Sony sensors and Sunny camera modules. The actuator inside those modules is still unnamed anywhere.

segments.title: Lidu Huang era filings
segments.text: Across Lidu Huang's tenure (Sep 2020-Apr 2025, 55.9 months) Meta filed a dense tunable-lens stack: wristband AF citing poLight (2022-01-04), two-stage wearable camera citing four CML documents (2022-05-31), macro-mode low-power AF (2022-07-12), 'flat-surfaced tunable optical lens' with PZT film for smart-glasses cameras (2022-07-22), the lens-barrel provisional (2022-07-26), retrieval of poLight's TLens Add-In pages (2022-10-19), an FPCB-mounted tunable lens (2022-11-08), the wide-FOV 107-degree/F2.2/TTL 5.0 mm assembly (2023-02-08) and closed-loop capacitance sensing (2023-08-28, the latest piezo priority). Seven piezo-relevant priorities in 20 months, with the window/polymer/glass-membrane/piezo stack described in TLens-like terms.

segments.title: Qualification, doubt and exits
segments.text: Jason Hartlove opened SPIE 2025 for Meta (2025-01); the CML-citing wearable camera was allowed 2025-01-21 and abandoned 2025-05-08. Huang left in April 2025 with a profile saying the piezo module passed 'full reliability qualifications for AR/VR/MR'; a forum claimed mass production that same month (rumor). Reality Labs' 2025-04-17 paper argued against autofocus in all-day glasses; the wide-FOV application took a final rejection on 2025-07-10; a new LC/electrowetting 'tunable lens camera module for AR glasses' was filed 2025-11-14; US 12,493,197 (macro AF, citing CML and poLight) was granted 2025-12-09. The record is strongest for a VR/MR camera and weakest for all-day glasses.

segments.title: Grants cluster before launch
segments.text: Allowance of the wide-FOV application (2026-02-23) was followed by a barrel-via continuation (2026-04-30), US 12,631,847 'lens barrel with an integrated tunable lens' (2026-05-19, expiring 2044-05-23) and US 12,663,619 (2026-06-23, 40.4 months after filing, citing three poLight documents); the continuation published 2026-09-17, six days before Connect. Patrick Llull joined from Apple as sensor-to-display architect (May 2026) and October 2026 job posts seek a camera-IQ lead for AI glasses/VR passthrough and a camera-system engineer owning modules 'through qualification and mass-production ramp', 146 days before the VR Glasses window. Further grants are possible Q4 2026-2027.

segments.title: Technology comparisons
segments.text: Karl Guttag's CES 2023 notes set CML's 8-wire SMA (~3.2 V/20 mA) against TLens's '<6 mW' (2023-03-04); Yole inferred a CML licence behind Alps's SMA production (2023-04-14); the VR market was 6.9m units in 2024 with Meta at ~77%; Everbright sized the TDK deal at 2,000+ patents and 2,000+ employees (2025-05-13). Nobody yet connected these actuators to a dated glasses launch.

segments.title: Sell-side turns to glasses
segments.text: A commissioned initiation valued poLight at NOK 9.0 (2026-02-06); Omdia counted 7.4m Meta AI glasses in 2025 (+281%) and >15m forecast for 2026 (2026-03-05); DBS's Meta note of 2026-05-08 never mentioned poLight. Within three days DBS published BUY on Q Tech (2026-08-26, TP HKD 12.60, 'low-power tunable lenses') and on Sunny Optical (2026-08-28, 'FY27 ramp of major smart-glasses programmes'); the Meta/Q Tech/poLight '1H27' sentence attributed to the gated Q Tech PDF the same day remains unverified. Everbright put Cowell's glasses mass production in 2026-2027.

segments.title: Secondary and AI-assistant noise
segments.text: Patsnap's liquid-lens landscape (2026-09-17) counts LG Innotek 7, Corning 5, Meta 3 and Apple 3 patents; Omdia put Meta at 3.4m AI glasses in 1H26 with 81.3% share (2026-09-22). The 2026-09-25 cluster of assistant outputs (62% TLens-in-VR-Glasses, 70% U.S.-OEM-is-Meta, a first production PO of NOK 5-15m by late Q4 2026/early Q1 2027, ~400k units year one) are model estimates, not sourced evidence, and one was retracted as 'too confident'. Omdia and TrendForce expect the XR market to shift to glasses from 2027, the backdrop every supplier is positioning for.

segments.title: Fixed-focus glasses, camera headsets
segments.text: Luxottica co-development began 2019-09-17; Quest 2 shipped 2020-10-13 without colour passthrough; Ray-Ban Stories (2021-09-09) were torn down as fixed focus with 'no voice coil or magnets'. Quest Pro (2022-10-25) and Quest 3 (teased 2023-06-01, shipped 2023-10-10, 131 days, 2x4 MP passthrough) added colour passthrough without autofocus, and Ray-Ban Meta shipped 20 days after its 2023-09-27 announcement. The pattern: glasses ship within weeks of announcement, headsets within months.

segments.title: Roadmap churn
segments.text: 'Puffin' was first reported on 2024-08-29 for 2027, pulled in to end-2026 (2025-06-02), delayed to H1 2027 (2025-12-06 memos) and confirmed by Bosworth on 2026-02-10 alongside Quest 4 'Griffin' (no earlier than H2 2027). Orion was shown 2024-09-25 with commercial AR 'expected 2027'; the EssilorLuxottica long-term deal (2024-09-17) and ~3% stake (2025-07-09) underpinned 2m Ray-Ban Meta by Feb 2025 and 7m AI glasses in 2025. Meta Ray-Ban Display shipped 13 days after its 2025-09-17 reveal (~84k units in 2025) and Gen 2 was confirmed 'simple fixed focus' on 2025-12-11.

segments.title: Connect 2026 and the autofocus line
segments.text: The own-brand Meta Glasses line launched 2026-06-23; Reality Labs lost US$4.62bn on US$431m revenue in Q2. Connect 2026 (2026-09-23) announced Meta VR Glasses at US$1,299.99 for spring 2027 with 'passthrough with autofocus and depth' (159-250 days announce-to-ship versus 13-34 days for glasses), shipped Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 the same day, and scheduled the camera-free Audio (2026-10-13) and Adventurer (2026-10-23). Bosworth said on 2026-09-24 there is 'no new version' of Display hardware and would not commit to AR glasses in 2027. The spring-2027 window therefore carries Meta's first and only documented autofocus camera.

segments.title: Vision Pro cycle, no actuator evidence
segments.text: Apple's tunable-lens patents (2018-09-21, 2023-05-03, 2023-07-21 with ex-CML CTO Topliss, 2024-03-12 with SMA) are all see-through prescription lenses, not camera autofocus. Vision Pro shipped 242 days after its 2023-06-05 announcement with 12 cameras and no actuator or module supplier identified; the M5 refresh shipped 7 days after announcement (2025-10-22) while production fell to 45,000 units in Q4 2025 from ~390,000 in 2024. The display-accessory glasses were paused Q4 2024 and cancelled January 2025.

segments.title: N50 slippage
segments.text: Gurman's targets moved from end-2026 (2025-05-23, with 'large quantities of prototypes' at end-2025) to reveal-2026/ship-2027 (2025-12-12), mass production December 2026 and launch early 2027 (2026-02-18), late 2027 (2026-05-31) and a WWDC June 2027 unveil with shipments by end-2027 (2026-07-26, reiterated 2026-09-27): about 12 months of slip over 492 days. The design has two camera sensors, capture and computer vision, with no autofocus reported; Kuo expects Q2 2027 mass production and 3-5m+ units in 2027, display glasses in 2029 and the N224 headset on 'life support'. Supplier-side evidence is thin: ex-CML CTO Ben Brown's move and SEMCO's coil deal point to Apple's existing actuator chain, not poLight.

segments.title: Platform assembly
segments.text: The Magic Leap partnership (May 2024, extended three years on 2025-10-30), Qualcomm's confirmation of joint glasses work (2024-09-05), Android XR's unveiling (2024-12-12), the US$250m HTC acqui-hire (2025-01-23) and Google I/O 2025 prototypes with Gentle Monster, Warby Parker (US$150m commitment) and Kering set the stage; Galaxy XR launched 2025-10-21 and Google said on 2025-12-08 'the first glasses will arrive next year'.

segments.title: 2026 launch, 2027 display
segments.text: Kering's CEO put Gucci glasses at 'probably next year, 2027' (2026-04-16); I/O 2026 (2026-05-19) committed Samsung/Google eyewear to 'this fall', display glasses to 2027 and Xreal Aura to before end-2026; Unpacked London (2026-07-22) formally introduced the eyewear and the FCC cleared SM-O200P/SM-O200J on 2026-10-01 with a Samsung official naming November 2026, 689 days after the Android XR unveil and 166 days after I/O. Nothing from Google addresses camera focus; the 2027 display generation is the window where any new camera module would be designed in.

segments.title: Headset first
segments.text: Joint OS/silicon/hardware design with Google and Qualcomm began in 2023; Project Moohan was named 2024-12-12 and shipped as Galaxy XR on 2025-10-31, ten days after its unveil, at US$1,799.99 with 2x6.5 MP passthrough plus 10 tracking cameras; an aggregator estimates ~40,000 units in 2025. No autofocus was claimed for the passthrough cameras.

segments.title: Glasses: a 19-month slip and an autofocus rumour
segments.text: ETNews reported 'Haean' glasses for 'later this year' on 2025-03-21; three weeks later the target became 2026, confirmed in the Q4-2025 earnings call, at MWC (2026-03-06, camera 'at your eye level'), at I/O (2026-05-19, 'this fall'), at Unpacked (2026-07-22) and by the FCC filing (2026-10-01: single 12 MP camera, AR1 Gen 1, 9 h) with a November 2026 launch, 590 days after the first report. VRARA's 2026-02-09 'early reports' of 12 MP with autofocus (234 days before the FCC filing) remain unconfirmed by Samsung; the leaked spec sheet names a Sony IMX681 at US$379-499. Samsung cites ~200 patent applications and a colour-display 'Haean' for 2027, possibly late 2027.

segments.title: Five Spectacles generations
segments.text: Spectacles shipped in 2016 (vending machines), 2018 (220,000 pairs cumulative by May 2018), 2019, 2021 (first AR display, developer-only) and 2024-09-17 (gen 5, 2 RGB + 2 IR cameras, 226 g, US$99/month for developers). Snap's IR release of 2025-06-10 committed to 'lightweight, immersive Specs in 2026', and Spectacles OS 2.0 (2025-09-15) promised a 'lighter and smaller' sixth generation 'next year'; Guttag called gen 5 'a developer kit, not a consumer product'.

segments.title: Consumer Specs
segments.text: Specs Inc. was formed 2026-01-28 and a multi-year Qualcomm deal signed 2026-04-10; AWE 2026 (2026-06-16, 371 days after the IR commitment) unveiled Specs at US$2,195, 51-degree FOV, 132/136 g, four cameras with no megapixel or focus figure; pre-orders opened 2026-09-16 (92 days later) with a US$200 deposit and shipping 'later this fall' in the US, UK and France, the initial run reportedly capped at ~100,000 units. As of 2026-10-06 specs.com still publishes no camera megapixel or focus specification, so the autofocus question for Specs is open.

segments.title: Display-glasses volume, flat units
segments.text: Xreal sold 137,200 glasses in 2023, 124,900 in 2024 and 133,700 in 2025 (revenue RMB 390m, 395m, 516m; adjusted net loss RMB 250m in 2025) and claimed 51% of worldwide AR share in Q3 2023. One Pro was promised for March 2025 and reached general availability on 2025-07-01, a 122-day slip; the Eye camera module shipped in July 2025 as 12 MP, f/2.25, 1.35 g and explicitly fixed focus, 'autofocus not supported'.

segments.title: Aura
segments.text: Project Aura was announced with Google on 2025-05-20, shown at AWE 2025 and CES 2026, and revealed in full at AWE 2026 (2026-06-16, 392 days later): 70-degree FOV, Snapdragon 'Reality Elite' puck, two tracking cameras plus one high-resolution camera of undisclosed focus type, no more than US$1,500, fall 2026 in five countries. A US$100m Series D (Jan 2026), an HKEX filing for up to US$400m (2026-04-01, Luxshare and Alibaba as shareholders) and a patent suit against Viture (2026-01-15) frame the launch; Android Authority's 2026-09-06 hands-on still said 'before the end of 2026'.

segments.title: From AR Lite to Rokid Glasses
segments.text: AR Lite (2024-04-23) was a display product; Rokid Glasses, unveiled 2024-11-14 for Q2 2025, reached Kickstarter only on 2025-08-26 (285 days later) with a 12 MP Sony IMX681 f/2.25 camera, passed US$1m in four days, closed at US$3.6m on 2025-10-10, exceeded US$4m by 2025-11-21 and delivered in November 2025, about five months late. Taiwan crowdfunding set a NT$62m record on 2025-12-12.

segments.title: Volume, fixed focus
segments.text: Ai Glasses Style (38.5 g, 12 MP Sony camera, US$299) was shown at CES on 2026-01-06, available globally 13 days later and past 15,000 units sold by 2026-02-02; Japan crowdfunding took ¥200m in ten days (2026-03-12). A 2026-07-30 review confirmed the camera is fixed focus with a 34 cm minimum distance, so Rokid's volume product carries no actuator at all. Rokid claims 41% of global AR and AI glasses shipments in H1 2026 (its own PR, 2026-09-28).

segments.title: X2 to X3 Pro
segments.text: RayNeo X2 went from CES 2023 to a China debut in November 2023 (~10 months); X2 Lite's 'Q3 2024' promise has no sourced ship date. X3 Pro (CES 2025-01-06) launched in China on 2025-05-27 (141 days) and globally on 2025-12-17 (345 days) with a 12 MP camera of unstated focus type; the V3 camera glasses promised at the same CES with '12 MP IMX681 with HDR and OIS', which would imply an actuator in a 39 g frame, have no ship date 638 days later. Counterpoint gave RayNeo 24% of global AR glasses in Q3 2025.

segments.title: Fast refresh, camera-free turn
segments.text: Air 4 Pro went from CES (2026-01-06) to sale in 19 days; the X3 Pro camera was confirmed as 12 MP IMX681 colour plus a monochrome 6DoF tracking camera on 2026-08-04, focus unstated; the camera-free iO, GT and GT Max were unveiled 2026-08-21 and retailed 14 days later, with X3 Pro cut to US$1,099. RayNeo claims the #1 global AR shipment position for H1 2026. Its newest products drop the camera entirely, the opposite of an autofocus roadmap.

segments.title: Camera-free by design
segments.text: G1 was unveiled 2024-06-26 and G2 (US$599) with the R1 ring followed 504 days later on 2025-11-12 with a 27.5-degree display and no cameras or speakers.

segments.title: Funding without cameras
segments.text: A US$150m pre-Series B at a US$1bn valuation (2026-07-06, Meituan and Tencent) was followed a day later by the CEO stating G3 'will not launch in 2026' and that cameras are not the company's direction; a software overhaul was promised within 1-3 months (2026-07-17). No addressable market for camera autofocus suppliers in 2026-2027.

segments.title: Audio frames
segments.text: Echo Frames generations 1 (2019-09-25, US$179.99), 2 (2020-11-19) and 3 (2023-09-20, from US$269.99) are audio-only with no camera or display, giving Amazon no consumer camera-glasses track record.

segments.title: Driver glasses and the Jayhawk rumour
segments.text: Reuters reported driver glasses 'Amelia' on 2024-11-11; The Information reported consumer 'Jayhawk' (camera plus monocular display) for late 2026/early 2027 on 2025-09-10, with no follow-up in the 391 days since. The delivery glasses with 'integrated cameras' were unveiled 2025-10-22 (763 days after Echo Frames 3), and the 2026-09-21 update counts 275,000 deliveries by 500+ drivers over 18 months, 5,000 more devices in 2026 and 20,000+ by end-2027, an order of magnitude below the rumoured 100,000 initial run. Amazon's AR patents cover UI and fulfilment, not optics or autofocus.

segments.title: Quark to Qwen
segments.text: Quark AI Glasses were previewed at WAIC on 2025-07-28 and launched 122 days later (2025-11-27; S1 from 3,799 yuan, G1 from 1,899 yuan, 12 MP, Qualcomm AR1); the renamed Qwen Glasses appeared at MWC 96 days after that (2026-03-03, 12 MP Sony IMX681) with China sales from 2026-03-08 and an international release 'within 2026' that has not yet been dated. Alibaba claimed 53% of China's online smart-glasses sales on 2026-05-08.

segments.title: N1 at 50 MP
segments.text: The N1 series was previewed on 2026-09-10, opened pre-orders 2026-09-22 and goes on sale 2026-10-13 (33 days preview-to-sale) with a 50 MP camera and iris payment, China only, 191 days after the Qwen Glasses drop. The 4-6-month cadence makes a mid-2027 successor likely but unannounced. The only tunable-lens trace in the Alibaba ecosystem is Ant Group's 'Look to Pay' demo glasses with a TLens camera (2026-08-06).

segments.title: Tunable-lens early adopter
segments.text: NEXTLENS was founded in Dietikon in June 2017; Xiaomi's Mitu Children's Learning Watch 4Pro (2020-01-07, 1,299 yuan) shipped an 8 MP 'T-LENS ultra-fast focus' camera, the first commercial poLight TLens product, and the Mi MIX Fold (2021-03-30) used a NEXTLENS liquid lens in its telephoto/macro camera.

segments.title: AI Glasses
segments.text: 36Kr reported a Goertek ODM partnership with Lei Jun expecting >300,000 units (2024-11-13); the AI Glasses launched 225 days later (2025-06-26) with a 12 MP Sony IMX681 and Snapdragon AR1 from 1,999 yuan, no autofocus claimed. IT Home's 2026-08-05 report of a completed-but-paused gen 2 slipping to Q4 2026 or 2027 was denied by Xiaomi, 405 days after launch; no supplier signal points at Xiaomi.

segments.title: Enterprise XR and the Magic Leap 2 proof
segments.text: Lenovo ThinkReality A3 (2021-01-10), the US$21.88bn IVAS award (2021-03-26), Pico 4 (2022-10-18), PS VR2 (2023-02-22) and Magic Leap 2 (2022-09-30) defined the period; Yole's teardown 153 days after ML2's release (2023-03-02) found poLight's TLens in its 13 MP camera, still the only teardown-confirmed TLens in an XR headset.

segments.title: Platform exits and pivots
segments.text: Microsoft discontinued HoloLens 2 (2024-10-01) and handed IVAS to Anduril (2025-02-11), which teamed with Meta on EagleEye (2025-05-29) and won US$159m (2025-09-09); HTC sold part of its XR division to Google (Jan 2025); Magic Leap partnered with Google (2024-05-30, extended 2025-10-29) and Pegatron (2025-12-30) before pivoting to waveguide supply (2026-07-09); Quanta put US$20m into Vuzix. The enterprise headset market that bought TLens via Magic Leap has largely dissolved into component supply.

segments.title: China AI-glasses wave, fixed focus
segments.text: Baidu's Xiaodu glasses took 364 days from unveil (2024-11-12) to sale; HTC Vive Eagle (12 MP, <49 g) went from announcement to Taiwan availability in 18 days (2025-08-14 to 2025-09-01); Meizu StarV Snap (2025-10-30), Mentra Live (Dec 2025) and INMO Air 3 (2025) list 12-16 MP cameras with no autofocus stated; Huawei's AI Glasses (2026-04-20, 12 MP, 35.5 g) came 23 months after its audio-only Eyewear 2 and 12 days after the tease. Across this wave no shipping product discloses an autofocus actuator.

segments.title: Headsets and enterprise autofocus wins
segments.text: SnkeXR named TLens in its medical AR headset on 2025-10-31; Valve announced Steam Frame on 2025-11-12 and released it 310 days later (2026-09-18) with four monochrome tracking cameras; Pico teased Project Swan on 2026-03-02, named it Space Pro, cancelled its 2026-09-02 event and moved release to Q4 2026 (a leak says early October at US$2,899); Ant Group showed 'Look to Pay' demo glasses with a TLens camera on 2026-08-06; Viture's Helix (12 MP, enterprise) ships Q1 2027. Vuzix booked follow-on orders on 2026-03-31, 2026-04-06, 2026-04-28 and 2026-08-11. Pico Space Pro is the one near-term headset where a 'VR VST TLens AF camera' could surface outside Meta.

headline_findings: Meta VR Glasses (spring 2027) is the only announced device with documented autofocus passthrough (2026-09-23); every supplier '2027' signal in the file converges on it, yet no primary source names the actuator supplier.

Program A's three qualification POs (2025-08-06, 2026-02-11, 2026-06-18; ~NOK 2.5m in total) fall 18.8, 12.6 and 8.4 months before 2027-03-01: the first precedes the usual 9–18-month qualification band, the second sits inside it, and the third lands at the band's near edge where production purchase orders would normally take over. poLight still calls the program 'qualification' and has never said 2027; a production PO in the Sep 2026–Feb 2027 band is the missing confirmation.

Program B became poLight's first consumer design-in on 2026-07-10 after four POs totalling NOK 4.9m over 228 days; with Q4 2026 deliveries and a 2026 launch, Samsung/Google (Nov 2026), Snap Specs and Xreal Aura (fall 2026) are the only matching camera-glasses windows, and none has disclosed its focus type; a Chinese ecosystem customer is also a live candidate, since poLight showed Ant Group 'Look to Pay' demo glasses with a TLens camera (Q2 2026 call) and Q Tech counts ten eyewear brands among its customers.

Q Tech's wording moved from 'US M brand vendor code' (2024-08-12) to 'small-batch deliveries for 2 leading overseas terminal clients' (2026-03-16) to 'TLens + AR Mono Engine: Volume Delivery Achieved... Ramp in 2H26/2027' (2026-08-24): a 161-day step from small-batch to volume that fits the 3-6-month pre-launch ramp for a late-2026 or spring-2027 device.

Meta's piezo tunable-lens patent stack (seven priorities Jan 2022-Aug 2023; grants 2025-12-09, 2026-05-19, 2026-06-23) cites poLight pages retrieved on 2022-10-19, and an ex-Meta engineer's profile says the module passed AR/VR/MR reliability qualification before Apr 2025: strong evidence of interest, but equally consistent with Meta having its own membrane lens built elsewhere.

Meta's Reality Labs paper of 2025-04-17 argued against autofocus in all-day glasses; Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 is documented fixed focus and no autofocus has been disclosed for Gen 3, Oakley Meta or Meta Ray-Ban Display, so TLens's 2027 Meta opportunity is the US$1,299.99 puck-powered VR Glasses, not the 7–10m-unit-per-year Ray-Ban line.

Cambridge Mechatronics' XR effort peaked between 2021-10-18 and 2024-01-29 (SF office, three SPIE talks, CES 2023) and has gone quiet: absent from SPIE 2025 and 2026, last XR article 2025-05-12 (512 days ago), CTO Ben Brown to Apple in Mar 2026, and Meta abandoned its CML-citing wearable-camera application on 2025-05-08.

Optotune's EL-3.1-10.8 (1.72 mm, 0.3 g, 20 mW at 10 dpt) launched 2026-09-21, 369 days after its handling instructions and two days before Connect 2026; it is the only non-poLight tunable lens with a glasses-class datasheet, but Optotune names no consumer customer and lists it for phones, action cams and robotics.

Apple's N50 has slipped about 12 months across 492 days of reporting (end-2026 on 2025-05-23 to end-2027 on 2026-09-27) and is described with two cameras and no autofocus; the only Apple-side actuator signals are ex-CML CTO Ben Brown's move (Mar 2026) and SEMCO's fine-pitch-coil deal (2025-12-17), both pointing away from TLens.

Among glasses that shipped in 2025-2026 every disclosed camera is fixed focus (Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2, Xreal Eye, Rokid Ai Glasses Style) or undisclosed (Snap Specs, Xreal Aura, Samsung SM-O200P, Alibaba N1 50 MP); the only teardown- or release-confirmed TLens XR wins remain Magic Leap 2 (2023-03-02), Vuzix Shield (2024-04-08) and SnkeXR (2025-10-31); the Ant Group demo glasses (2026-08-06) are a fourth, pre-product sighting.

The DBS 'Meta + Q Tech + poLight, 1H27' sentence (2026-08-26) is timing-consistent with a spring-2027 launch (module mass production 2-4 months before), but it is unverified, absent from DBS's public summary and from DBS's own 2026-05-08 Meta note.

The next hard checkpoints are poLight's Q3 report (2026-10-29) and Capital Markets Day (2026-10-30), Samsung's November launch, Snap and Xreal fall shipments, and poLight's Q4 report on 2027-02-24, five days before the VR Glasses window opens; a Program A production PO several times the ~NOK 2.5m of qualification orders to date would be the first non-circumstantial link.

poLight reported no new PZT MEMS wafers ordered or delivered through 30 June 2026 (annual report 2025; Q2 2026 report); because wafer starts at STMicroelectronics precede volume assembly by roughly 6–9 months, a wafer order in Q3–Q4 2026 is a harder precondition for spring-2027 volumes than any purchase-order wording, and the Q3 report on 2026-10-29 is the first place it would surface.

Open contradiction to watch: the Phoenix supply-chain preview names Sunny Optical for camera modules while the TLens trail runs through Q Tech; both are compatible with TLens only if poLight's 'support all camera-module partners' stance applies, and Sunny's own August 2026 deck lists a 'Compact High-Res AF' camera for AR glasses without naming the actuator.
critique:
analysts | 12 of 34 events (analysts-9-80..9-104: "Assistant probability table ~62%", "User creates scheduled task", "User uploads screenshot", "Assistant 2027-2029 revenue scenarios") are chat-trace artefacts, not market events; analysts-9-104 is dated 2027 and analysts-9-105 (Omdia forecast) is dated by forecast year, so both sort as future events | Move them to a separate "research-log" lane or drop; re-date forecasts to publication date (Omdia 2026-09-22); keep only sourced analyst notes (DBS, Omdia, Counterpoint, Everbright, Patsnap)

polight | Massive cross-digest duplication: the 2025-10-13 NOK 5m PO appears 6 times (polight-1-0, 4-48, 6-76, 7-28, 8-54, 9-36), each Program A/B PO 3-4 times; 179 events and 74 "key" flags are inflated and the same applies to metaip (US 12,663,619 grant = metaip-6-63/8-70/9-56) and windows (VR Glasses spring 2027 = w-meta-0-8/3-14/4-12/6-3/7-9/8-9/9-0; CMD = w-polight-4-6/7-4/8-6; DBS = w-analysts-4-13/7-8/9-1) | Run a dedupe pass on (lane, date, normalised title) keeping the best-sourced copy and merging ids; report true counts

polight | Finding 2 is arithmetically inconsistent: 18.8 and 8.4 months are outside the stated 9-18-month qualification band, yet the finding says all three POs are "inside" it | Rewrite: PO #1 precedes the band, PO #2 sits inside, PO #3 sits in the 3-9-month ramp zone; or justify a wider band from the Magic Leap 2 / Vuzix Shield precedents in the file

polight | Precondition missing from findings: AR2025 (polight-6-74) and Q2 2026 (polight-9-49) both say no new MEMS wafers were ordered, manufactured or delivered; a spring-2027 volume launch needs ST wafer orders roughly 6-9 months ahead, so "no wafers by 30 Jun 2026" is a stronger timing signal than any PO | Add a derived window "poLight wafer order to ST (Q3-Q4 2026)" and a checkpoint on the Q3 report (2026-10-29): search report text for "wafer"; query ST thin-film PZT lead times

meta | Finding 6 asserts Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 "remains fixed focus" but no event supports it (meta-0-69 lists only 12MP/3K/9 h); only Gen 2 is documented fixed focus (meta-0-44) | Query Meta/Ray-Ban Gen 3 spec page and reviews (PCMag, The Verge, DCW) for "autofocus"/"fixed focus"; same for Meta Ray-Ban Display and Oakley Vanguard cameras, whose teardowns (meta-7-27, meta-7-22) give no AF detail

otheroem | Confirmed TLens XR sighting omitted from finding 10: Ant Group "Look to Pay" demo glasses shown with TLens camera (otheroem-4-87, 2026-08-06); combined with Rokid-Ant International partnership (rokid-2-62) and Q Tech's "10 brands" eyewear customers (qtech-7-36), a Chinese OEM is a live Program B candidate that finding 3 silently excludes | Add Ant glasses to the TLens-wins list; search Ant Group / Rokid / Alibaba glasses for "TLens" or "自动对焦 MEMS"; map polight onto w-alibaba-3-3 and a Rokid window

modules | Contradiction not addressed: the Phoenix supply-chain preview (modules-0-65) names Sunny Optical for camera modules, while the TLens story runs through Q Tech; Sunny H1-2026 also lists a "Compact High-Res AF" smart-glasses module (modules-7-53, truncated) with an unnamed actuator | Read Sunny Optical H1 2026 results deck for the AF module's actuator type; check whether modules-0-65 distinguishes passthrough from tracking cameras; query "舜宇 智能眼镜 自动对焦 模组"

qtech | Finding 4 conflates signals: "Volume Delivery Achieved" for TLens in H1 2026 is 9-12 months before spring 2027, well ahead of the 2-4-month module-MP norm, and fits a 2026 product (Program B) better than VR Glasses; the "US M brand vendor code" (2024) covers Q Tech's pancake lenses and modules generally, not TLens | Split the Q Tech signals by product (TLens vs AR Mono Engine vs pancake lens) using the H1-2026 deck pages; downgrade the vendor-code match

metaip | Tension unexamined: Lidu Huang's profile says Meta's piezo tunable-lens module passed AR/VR/MR reliability qualification before Apr 2025, yet Program A "qualification" POs only start Aug 2025; either Program A is not Meta, or the Aug-2025 POs are second-source (Q Tech line) qualification, which poLight-9-28 ("demanded dual-source") hints at | Add this as an explicit finding; search Meta job postings 2025-2026 for "tunable lens"/"piezo" camera roles and current employers of the other inventors (Xiong et al.)

samsung | samsung-1-56 (VRARA, "early reports" of 12MP with autofocus) contradicts findings 3 and 10 ("none has disclosed its focus type"); also Haean display glasses 2027 (w-samsung-1-18/1-19) has no supplier mapping while w-google-1-13 (same device family) does | Check FCC internal photos / Samsung spec page for SM-O200P "autofocus"; add w-samsung-1-18 to the lead-time windows with the same suppliers as w-google-1-13

rayneo | No forward window for the #1 AR-glasses vendor (all three RayNeo windows are 2024-2025), and the V3 camera glasses "12MP IMX681 with OIS" (rayneo-2-81) ship status is unknown; if V3 shipped it is the first glasses camera with a moving-lens actuator, directly relevant to the VCM/SMA-in-glasses question | Search JD.com/Tmall "雷鸟 V3" listing and spec; add RayNeo X3 successor / CES 2027 rumours as a window
